tools.name: spellkave_orient
tools.label: Spellkave Orient
tools.description: Rebuild your situation from the world in one call: self/scene/in-world turn-scene/manipulation and sensing facts plus inventory and the MOST RECENT page of traces — the one thing an actor with no history legitimately needs (a fresh conversation, a reloaded world, a restarted host). Freely callable mid-run too, as a situation refresh. Traces are bounded and page most-recent-first, never the whole history at once; pass the returned traces.next_cursor back as cursor to go further back, one page per call. view.manipulation_context uses the same snake_case rows as spellkave_manipulation_context (a prompts[] row from either is the same semantic_context); its actions are bounded to the most relevant rows (answers to open prompts first, then authored cues and defaults, then input forms, then alphabetical) with actions_total, actions_more and actions_by_niche saying what was left out — call spellkave_manipulation_context for more_action_ids (every other action id) and pass action_ids there for the syntax rows of named actions.

cursor.description: Opaque traces.next_cursor from a prior spellkave_orient call — fetches the NEXT (older) page of traces. Omit for the first call: the most recent page, which stands alone as a usable orientation.

limit.description: Traces per page (default 10, max 25). Going further back costs more calls, deliberately — recall should cost turns, not one unbounded dump.

argumentGates: Caller-owned acting context only; presence is nonspatial and conveys no NPC consent.

tools.name: spellkave_status
tools.label: Spellkave Status
tools.description: Read current Spellkave world status from the SDK snapshot.

tools.name: spellkave_events
tools.label: Spellkave Events
tools.description: Read recent Spellkave world events from the SDK snapshot. The `spellkave_events` tool no longer lists another session's session lifecycle, in-session frame, turn-boundary, or action-economy header rows for unrelated plain players; participants and callers with an extent grant that covers a participant still see those rows.

limit.description: Maximum number of recent events to read.

tools.name: spellkave_self_summary
tools.label: Spellkave Self Summary
tools.description: Compact directly-controlled character summary — the RECURRING glance you re-fetch often (vitals/quest/conditions/capabilities), not a one-time sheet. Identity is the connected actor; no actor id is accepted. `conditions`, `vitals`, `quest`, and `capabilities` are each a bounded-collection envelope: `listing` is "complete" when `items` holds the whole authorized collection, or "examples" when it is a bounded slice with a machine-readable `continuation` {tool, args} for the rest. `vitals` and `quest` are world-driven: which states appear (and in what order) depends on the character; a character with no quest-tracking states correctly shows an empty `quest` bucket. Call spellkave_self_states with kind=state for the full authorized state set. `capabilities` holds the actor's own trained/granted capabilities; call spellkave_self_states with kind=capability for the full authorized set. Recent evaluation history (own rolls and check outcomes) is not part of this summary — call spellkave_self_states with kind=evaluation for it; act-tool results already carry the roll from the action that produced it. Identity (species/class/background/…) is not part of this summary either — it is static character data, not something that changes turn to turn, so it lives at spellkave_self_states with kind=identity: fetch that ONCE at session start for the detailed "who am I", and rely on this summary for everything that actually changes.

tools.name: spellkave_self_states
tools.label: Spellkave Self Sheet
tools.description: Page through the connected actor's authorized state pools, conditions, capabilities, identity facets, recent evaluation history, or action-economy channel spends. Use kind=condition for condition continuation, kind=capability for the actor's own trained/granted capabilities, kind=identity for the actor's own species/class/background tags (static session-entry detail, with descriptions where the world declared them; fetch this once at session start rather than on every turn), kind=evaluation for the actor's own recent check outcomes (status and any resolved rolls — e.g. what a check rolled), most-recent-first, kind=economy for the actor's own action-economy channel standing (per channel: current-window spent_ms/window_start_ms, plus the last spend's cost_ms/remaining_ms — "how much of my turn is left"). State rows support authored state-id prefix and exact resource-tag filters. Evaluation rows support an exact provenance_id filter to look up a specific record (e.g. from an act receipt). Use next_cursor to continue.

kind.description: Self-sheet row kind. Defaults to state.

state_prefix.description: Exact state_id prefix filter; valid only for kind=state.

state_tag.description: Exact authored resource tag filter; valid only for kind=state.

provenance_id.description: Exact provenance_id filter; valid only for kind=evaluation. Returns matched 1 and the row, or matched 0.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor from the prior page.

tools.name: spellkave_scene
tools.label: Spellkave Scene
tools.description: Orient on the connected actor's authorized current scene (location implicit). Unfiltered and under the bound, returns EVERY authorized target (`listing: "complete"`) alongside authored node prose (`node_description`, `graph_description`, `pose_elevation`) and occupant/entity/exit/trace `counts`. `graph_description` is carried only the first time this session sees the current region, or again after a call returns to a DIFFERENT region than the previous scene read — repeated reads within the same region carry `graph_description: null` instead of repeating the identical blurb. Add a `kind` filter, exceed the bound, or pass a `cursor` and it falls back to a flat, revision-bound paged list (`listing: "paginated"`) carrying the SAME handles and the SAME node prose/counts. Each `exit` row carries its destination as `to` (shortened when it stays in the same region — full path only across a region switch), so spellkave_scene_detail is only needed for an exit's extra detail, not to learn where it leads. Each item carries its OWN stable `handle`+`rev`: the SAME actor/entity/exit/trace keeps the SAME handle across scene re-reads and ticks, for as long as it exists, even while unrelated targets in the same scene change; `rev` gates freshness of that ONE target only. Follow up on any handle with spellkave_scene_detail or spellkave_move (rev+handle mode) by copying that item's OWN `rev`+`handle` verbatim — never the envelope's top-level `rev` — and the same stale_handle rejection applies at either: the loop closes at act, not at this observe call, and other actors may move between the two. While you are on a journey the answer is still the place you left and carries journey {status, arrives_in_ticks, arrives_at_tick}; pass wait_for_arrival_ms to wait for the arrival in one call instead of polling.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor from the prior page.

wait_for_arrival_ms.description: Optional. While you are on a journey (a move that takes several ticks), wait up to this many milliseconds for it to end, then answer with the scene as it is then. Returns at once when you are not travelling; the host may cap the wait, and journey_wait says how it ended. Use this instead of re-reading the scene or the session status until you arrive.

examples.description: replace PLAYER_PROFILE to start or reuse a session and orient in the scene

argumentGates: Caller-owned acting context only; presence is nonspatial and conveys no NPC consent.

tools.name: spellkave_scene_detail
tools.label: Spellkave Scene Detail
tools.description: Read one current authorized scene target by its OWN rev+handle (copy both verbatim from that target's own listing row — not the listing envelope's top-level `rev`). The handle is a stable identity: the SAME exit/actor/entity/trace keeps the SAME handle across arbitrarily many scene re-reads and ticks, for as long as it exists, even while unrelated targets in the same scene change. `rev` gates freshness of that ONE target only — a rev mismatch (`stale_handle`) means THIS target's own content changed since the handle was issued; a handle that no longer resolves at all (`unknown_handle`) means the target left this actor's authorized scene (moved away, removed, out of range). An `actor` target's `detail` additionally carries `description` (authored flavor prose, `""` if none), `appearance` (the public appearance text the character wrote at creation, `""` if none), `entity_def_id` (its authored definition id — the SAME field the `entity` scene target already carries, `""` if unresolved), and `conditions` (the SAME visibility-filtered status effects `spellkave_self_states kind=condition` surfaces for the connected actor's own body, `[]` if none). Two addressing modes: {handle, rev} copied from the listing (freshness-gated), or target_id — the same typed id spellkave_manipulate takes (entity:156, item:157, actor:7) — which reads the current row and returns its rev. Entity and actor detail includes contents {container_ref, scope: "direct", revision, status, items}; status is available, empty, unavailable or truncated, with no hidden total. Items carry canonical item:N target_ref, parent_ref, name, quantity and entity_def_id. Inspect a disclosed child with target_id, including nested containers; these children do not become room occupants. Contents changes affect the target revision, and closing an ancestor revokes its descendants. Visibility does not promise pickup success or grant personal inventory state.

rev.description: The target's OWN rev, copied verbatim from its row in spellkave_scene — not the listing envelope's top-level rev (stable per-target handles, freshness gated per target).

handle.description: Stable scene target handle, e.g. s:exit:32 or s:actor:7 — copied from spellkave_scene.

tools.name: spellkave_map
tools.label: Map
tools.description: Render the connected actor's OWN known map as the shared spatial view — fog-of-war scoped by the module's visible_place_* views (known places plus the current place's exit frontier). Routes admitted by the module are drawn; spellkave_scene stays the authority on what exits exist from the CURRENT place. output_type picks the ONE artifact computed and returned: 'utf8' box-drawing text, 'ascii' 7-bit text, 'braille' dense-dot text, 'inventory' the place/route listing alone, 'svg' (default) the raw picture (plus an inline picture for hosts that render tool images), 'jpg' a backdrop-composed map-art JPEG written to disk (details.jpg_path). On the hosted PLAYER MCP gateway, results may also include one text line linking to the interactive browser map (maps.spellkave.com/?world=<slug>) for this world. While you are in a fight with a tactical grid drawn, the response also carries session_tokens: one row per roster participant placed on a drawn cell (node_id, actor_id, name, and is_me for your own row) — absent outside a fight, an empty list the moment the fight opens but before anyone has taken a cell.

graph.description: Optional map id — when set, draw that map restricted to places the connected actor has already seen. Omit and the map picks for you: while you are in a fight that opened a tactical grid, it draws THAT grid composed over the location you are fighting in (backdrop art plus the room's own layout, combat cells on top); otherwise it composes every known outdoor map. Naming a map explicitly always wins — pass the location's own id to see the region while a fight is open, or compose_parent=false for the bare grid.

slice.description: How to project multi-floor / unpositioned maps: elevation_band (one floor), all_floors_offset (floors side-by-side), topology_only (adjacency layout), metric (all z in one plane), h3_world (outdoor maps laid out geographically). Omit for auto.

compose_parent.description: Default true. When graph= names the battle map of an active fight, the grid draws composed over its parent location's own known layout (and, for output_type='jpg', the parent's backdrop art too) — one picture, the battle grid in room context. Has no effect for a non-grid graph= (or when graph= is omitted). Set false for the grid alone when you specifically want just the battle grid with no surrounding room.

z_tolerance.description: Half-width of elevation_band in elevation units (default 0.5).

output_type.description: Which single artifact to render — the engine computes ONLY this one. 'utf8' box-drawing text, 'ascii' 7-bit text, 'braille' dense-dot text — each returned in the like-named details field. 'inventory' skips the picture entirely, details.inventory only. 'svg' (default) returns the raw SVG string in details.svg (and, when the host renders tool-result images, an inline picture). 'jpg' writes a backdrop-composed JPEG to output_dir/output_name and returns its path as details.jpg_path — no svg/ascii/utf8/braille text in the response at all.

output_dir.description: output_type='jpg' only; ignored otherwise. Host-supplied directory to write the map-art JPEG into — absolute, or RELATIVE to the host process's own cwd. A relative value resolves against process.cwd() for the write, and is echoed back UNCHANGED — never resolved — in details.jpg_path, so a caller recording a portable artifact never leaks its own machine-local checkout path. Optional: omit for a fresh temp directory — a caller that just wants 'a JPEG, anywhere' does not have to invent a path. Backdrop art is drawn in full (the map on top stays scoped to places already seen, but the backdrop itself is NOT masked, so it may show rooms not yet discovered).

output_name.description: output_type='jpg' only; ignored otherwise. Base filename (no extension) for the JPEG written under output_dir, e.g. 'arrival'. Optional: omit for a name derived from graph, or 'map' when graph itself is also omitted.

tools.promptSnippet: Draw the places you have already seen (fog of war)
promptGuidelines: Shows places and routes the module admits for this caller (known + current exit frontier) — spellkave_scene stays the source of truth for what's here RIGHT NOW and which exits the CURRENT place has.
Indoor/multi-floor: pass graph= and slice=elevation_band with z= (default auto z=0), or slice=all_floors_offset for side-by-side floors.
Omit graph to compose every known outdoor map.

The default (svg) gives an inline picture where the host renders tool images; output_type=jpg saves a map-art file; output_type=utf8/ascii/braille/inventory are the cheap text reads — pick one of those when a picture would be wasted.

tools.name: spellkave_move
tools.label: Spellkave Move
tools.description: Move the active actor — exactly one addressing mode per call. Preferred: {rev, handle}, a stable-identity scene exit handle copied VERBATIM (both fields) from that exit's own row in spellkave_scene — the SAME exit keeps the SAME handle across re-reads and ticks; `rev` gates freshness of that ONE exit only, never the whole scene. Compatibility: {edge_id}, an adjacent-exit identifier when you do not have a scene handle. Movement is ATTEMPT-based: every exit is tried, and the world gives the authoritative verdict. The scene listing's `traversal_gates` and this tool's own `traversal_gates` echo (rev+handle mode only) are map info about what LOOKED likely, never permission. In rev+handle mode, the result carries `receipt` (what the world did) and a sibling `observation` (prose of what the actor perceived — an authored node description, or the region's own description only when the move crossed into a different region, never repeated within the same one — or null + observation_gap when no authorized source backs this outcome); a rejection carries `receipt.move.reason` and `receipt.move.failure_detail`, never a throw. In edge_id mode, the result is a flatter `{status, actor_id, edge_id, from_node, to_node, observed_at_tick}` shape, with `reason`/`failure_detail` on rejection. Movement is never turn-gated: a move may be accepted even while `my_turn` is false. In rev+handle mode, on an ADMITTED dispatch (an immediate arrival OR a promoted long-running 'travelling' walk) with a host world-event builder wired, the result also carries `consequences`: same-tick, same-transaction WorldEvents THIS move deterministically caused (e.g. a travel-cost resource spend) — a THIRD register, distinct from `receipt`/`observation` (the reducer's own outcome) and from a LATER `pushes` drain off the same builder (world news, including this move's own delayed arrival). Omitted entirely when no builder is wired; `[]` when wired but nothing was caused. A move longer than your reach returns outcome "travelling" and takes several ticks: pass wait_for_arrival_ms to wait for the arrival in the same call, or spellkave_scene with wait_for_arrival_ms to keep waiting; do not poll.

rev.description: Scene-handle mode: the exit's OWN rev, copied verbatim from its row in spellkave_scene — not the listing envelope's top-level rev. Required together with handle; omit both and pass edge_id instead for the adjacent-exit mode.

handle.description: Scene-handle mode: stable scene exit handle, e.g. s:exit:32, from spellkave_scene. Required together with rev; omit both and pass edge_id instead for the adjacent-exit mode.

edge_id.description: Adjacent-exit mode: identifier of an adjacent exit from where you are. Prefer rev+handle instead — this mode exists when you do not have a scene handle.

wait_for_arrival_ms.description: Optional, scene-handle mode. A move longer than your reach becomes a journey of several ticks (outcome "travelling"). With this field the call waits up to that many milliseconds for the journey to end and then returns the arrival observation; journey says whether you arrived, were stopped elsewhere, or are still travelling (the host may cap the wait). Without it the call returns as soon as the journey starts.

tools.name: spellkave_inventory
tools.label: Spellkave Inventory
tools.description: Orient on the connected actor's authorized carried inventory. Unfiltered and under the bound, returns a grouped tree of top-level possessions with nested `contents` and `equipped_slot` markers. Add a kind/name_prefix filter, exceed the bound, or pass a cursor and it falls back to a flat, revision-bound paged list carrying the SAME handles the tree uses. Every response self-describes via `listing` ('complete' for the tree, 'paginated' for the flat fallback). Each item carries its OWN stable `handle`+`rev`: the SAME item keeps the SAME handle across re-reads, for as long as it exists, regardless of tree position or what else in the inventory changed. Follow up on any handle with spellkave_item_detail by copying that item's OWN `rev`+`handle` verbatim — never the envelope's top-level `rev`.

kind.description: Optional exact authored entity kind filter. Forces the flat paged list.

name_prefix.description: Optional case-insensitive item-name prefix filter. Forces the flat paged list.

limit.description: Maximum items per page, and the unfiltered grouped-tree threshold. Defaults to 50.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor from a prior paged response. Forces the flat paged list.

tools.name: spellkave_item_detail
tools.label: Spellkave Item Detail
tools.description: Inspect one item selected by its OWN rev+handle from spellkave_inventory (copy both verbatim from that item's own row — not the listing envelope's top-level `rev`). The handle is the item's stable identity: the SAME item keeps the SAME handle across re-reads, for as long as it exists, regardless of tree position or what else in the inventory changed. Returns authorized identity, quantity, containment/equipment role, and owned state in one call; arbitrary item ids are not accepted. Two addressing modes: {handle, rev} copied from the listing (freshness-gated), or target_id — the same typed id spellkave_manipulate takes (entity:156, item:157, actor:7) — which reads the current row and returns its rev.

rev.description: The item's OWN rev, copied verbatim from its row in spellkave_inventory — not the listing envelope's top-level rev (stable per-item handles, freshness gated per item).

handle.description: Stable inventory item handle, e.g. i:42 — copied from spellkave_inventory.

tools.name: spellkave_trace_detail
tools.label: Spellkave Trace Detail
tools.description: Read one currently perceived trace by its OWN rev+handle (copy both verbatim from that trace's own row — not the listing envelope's top-level `rev`). The handle is the trace's stable identity: the SAME trace keeps the SAME handle across re-reads, for as long as it stays perceivable, regardless of what else was inscribed since. Returns parsed payload, never the raw payload JSON carrier.

rev.description: The trace's OWN rev, copied verbatim from its row in spellkave_traces — not the listing envelope's top-level rev (stable per-trace handles, freshness gated per trace).

handle.description: Stable trace handle, e.g. t:4 — copied from spellkave_traces.

tools.name: spellkave_session_status
tools.label: Spellkave Session Status
tools.description: Summarize the connected actor's in-world turn/scene (not the MCP connection): lifecycle, roster order, and whose turn it is. Accepts no session or actor id. `no_session` still allows exploration. The orientation tool also includes this in-world session state.

limit.description: Ongoing sessions per page; implies detail.

cursor.description: Continuation from ongoing.next_cursor; implies detail. Restart without cursor if the list changes.

detail.description: Include authorized operation details and world-tick timing, including initiated and external-wait phases.

session_id.description: Read details for a previously observed session, including its terminal state. Requires participation; implies detail.

tools.name: spellkave_reaction_options
tools.label: Spellkave Reaction Options
tools.description: List the connected actor's open reaction seats with deadline and originating context. Uses revision-bound reaction handles; raw pending ids are never exposed.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor from the prior page.

tools.name: spellkave_intervention_windows
tools.label: Spellkave Intervention Windows
tools.description: List the connected actor's OPEN post-roll intervention windows — a time-boxed pause after one of the actor's own stochastic actions, before the outcome commits. `faces` are the already-drawn, already-visible die face(s) for that action (two faces when the roll had Advantage/Disadvantage, otherwise one). The window closes on its own (equivalent to declining) if not answered before window_closes_at_micros. Respond with spellkave_react_option using this listing's handle: omit selected_draw_index to decline (the original result stands, nothing is spent), or pass the index of one listed face to accept (spends this window's fuel resource and replaces exactly that face — the new roll must then be used).

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor from the prior page.

tools.name: spellkave_react_option
tools.label: Spellkave React Option
tools.description: Execute one current handle for the connected actor — either a multi-actor reaction seat from spellkave_reaction_options, or a post-roll intervention window from spellkave_intervention_windows. For an intervention-window handle, omit selected_draw_index to decline (keep the original result, spend nothing) or pass the index of one of that window's listed faces to accept (spends its fuel resource and replaces exactly that face; the new roll must then be used). The handle only selects; the world independently revalidates sender, eligibility, and the window. On dispatch, the result carries `receipt` (what the world did) and a sibling `observation` (prose of what the actor perceived, or null + observation_gap when no authorized source backs this outcome). On a SUCCESSFUL dispatch with a host world-event builder wired, the result also carries `consequences`: same-tick, same-transaction WorldEvents THIS reaction deterministically caused — a THIRD register, distinct from `receipt`/`observation` (the reducer's own outcome) and from a LATER `pushes` drain off the same builder (world news, e.g. another agent's subsequent move). Omitted entirely when no builder is wired; `[]` when wired but nothing was caused.

rev.description: Current reaction-window or intervention-window revision (matches the handle's domain).

handle.description: A handle from spellkave_reaction_options (e.g. r2) or spellkave_intervention_windows (e.g. w0).

response_intent.description: Authored or free-text response intent passed to the typed reaction reducer.

selected_draw_index.description: Intervention windows only: the index (into that window's `faces`) of the already-drawn face to replace. Omit to decline — the original result stands and nothing is spent. Providing an index accepts: it spends the window's fuel resource and replaces exactly that one face; the new roll must then be used. Ignored (and should be omitted) for a plain spellkave_reaction_options seat.

tools.name: spellkave_suggest_next_action
tools.label: Spellkave Suggest Next Action
tools.description: Read a deterministic Spellkave suggestion or affordance summary from SDK state. Does not submit reducers.

entity_ref.description: EntityRef of the perceiver body to suggest for — not `Actor.actor_id` (the steering principal). Accepts a bare numeric entity id (`42`), `entity:42`, `item:42` (an item is still an entity row; same numeric id), or a manifest key suffix (`core/player`).

tools.name: spellkave_manipulation_context
tools.label: Spellkave Manipulation Context
tools.description: Read your additive factored manipulation context: shared authored action syntax, independently observed typed targets, and complete participant expectations. These are neutral discovery facts, not a list of action-target offers and not a promise that an attempt will succeed. Use them to compose one typed manipulation attempt; the world authoritatively reselects and validates it against fresh state. The default answer is a bounded summary: prompts[], targets[], participants[], the most relevant action rows in actions[] (answers to open prompts first, then authored cues and defaults, then input forms, then alphabetical), and more_action_ids naming every other action you may attempt. Pass action_ids to read the syntax rows of named actions; detail="full" returns the whole registry and is large. prompts[] lists the open dialogue prompts you may answer now (question, labels, responseActionIds; multi-pick questions state the remaining picks, this one included); answering one means sending its responseActionId with that row as args_json {"semantic_context": <row>}. A prompt opens one to three ticks after the answer that leads to it; pass wait_for_prompt_ms to wait for it in one call instead of polling. It waits for a prompt only: it is not a way to wait for a journey or a turn.

detail.description: Optional, default "summary": prompts[], targets[], participants[], the most relevant action rows (answers to open prompts first, then authored cues and defaults, then input forms, then alphabetical) as composition syntax, and more_action_ids naming every other action. "full" returns every action row with provider flags, template ids, groups and tags; it grows with the actor's capabilities (100 KB for a spellcaster) and is meant for programmatic readers.

action_ids.description: Optional, summary only: action ids (from more_action_ids, a prompt's response_action_ids, or a hint) whose syntax rows to return first in actions[]. Ids the listing does not hold come back in unknown_action_ids.

wait_for_prompt_ms.description: Optional. When prompts[] holds no open, unanswered prompt yet, wait up to this many milliseconds for one to open before returning (a prompt opens one to three ticks after the answer that leads to it). Returns as soon as one opens, or at the deadline with prompts[] as it is then; the host may cap the wait. Omit for an immediate read.

argumentGates: Caller-owned acting context only; presence is nonspatial and conveys no NPC consent.

tools.name: spellkave_entity
tools.label: Spellkave Entity
tools.description: Read an entity's identity row by entity_id (numeric id, 'entity:N', or a manifest key) — entity_def_id, name, kind, and stack quantity — or null if it does not resolve. General-purpose quantity surface outside the PLAYER inventory flow (e.g. verifying a coin stack shrank by a purchase price, or a purchased ware landed with the right count); spellkave_inventory and spellkave_item_detail also carry quantity, while spellkave_entity_container exposes containment only, never quantity.

entity_id.description: Entity identifier (numeric id, 'entity:N', or a manifest key). Returns its identity row — entity_def_id, name, kind, and stack quantity — or null if it does not resolve. General-purpose quantity surface outside the PLAYER inventory flow (spellkave_inventory and spellkave_item_detail also carry quantity); spellkave_entity_container returns containment only, never quantity.

tools.name: spellkave_entity_container
tools.label: Spellkave Entity Container
tools.description: Read the container that holds a given entity, or null if it is not contained.

entity_id.description: Contained entity identifier. Returns the container that holds it, or null if it is not contained.

tools.name: spellkave_observer_knowledge
tools.label: Spellkave Observer Knowledge
tools.description: Read an observer body's knowledge of entities. Body-keyed fog-of-war view; use the place and trace knowledge tools for those domains.

observer_id.description: Observer body entity identifier. Returns what that body has perceived (entities, affordances, traces).

tools.name: spellkave_observer_place_knowledge
tools.label: Spellkave Observer Place Knowledge
tools.description: Read the place nodes an observer body has perceived. Body-keyed fog-of-war view.

observer_id.description: Observer body entity identifier. Returns the place nodes that body has perceived.

tools.name: spellkave_observer_trace_knowledge
tools.label: Spellkave Observer Trace Knowledge
tools.description: Read the inscribed traces an observer body has perceived (seam A inscription-time + seam B arrival scan — ADR-0040). Body-keyed fog-of-war view.

observer_id.description: Observer body entity identifier. Returns the inscribed-trace knowledge that body has perceived (seam A + seam B — ADR-0040).

tools.name: spellkave_traces
tools.label: Spellkave Traces
tools.description: Orient on perceived traces at the connected actor's current node (location implicit). Items are MOST-RECENT-FIRST (highest inscribed_at first) — page 0 is what just happened here, matching spellkave_orient.traces; pass next_cursor to walk further back. Unfiltered and under the bound, returns EVERY perceived trace (`listing: "complete"`) alongside a capped-and-truthful `by_kind` histogram (`kind_groups_total`/`kind_groups_shown`/`kind_groups_truncated`) computed over ALL perceived traces at this node, regardless of any filter you pass. Add a `kind`/`kind_prefix`/`inscribed_by`/`visibility` filter, exceed the bound, or pass a `cursor` and it falls back to a flat, revision-bound paged list (`listing: "paginated"`) carrying the SAME handles, node id, and the SAME global `by_kind` histogram — filtering `items` never narrows `by_kind`. Raw payload JSON is never returned; use spellkave_trace_detail for parsed payload. Each item carries its OWN stable `handle`+`rev`: the SAME trace keeps the SAME handle across re-reads for as long as it stays perceivable, and `rev` gates freshness of that ONE trace only — copy both verbatim into spellkave_trace_detail, not the envelope's top-level `rev`.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor from the prior page.

argumentGates: Caller-owned acting context only; presence is nonspatial and conveys no NPC consent.

tools.name: spellkave_entity_body
tools.label: Spellkave Entity Body
tools.description: Read the body row for an entity, or null if it has none.

entity_id.description: Entity identifier. Returns its body row, or null if it has none.

tools.name: spellkave_communicate
tools.label: Spellkave Communicate
tools.description: Attempt one authored speech act against one typed target. Use an observed participant or world target and an authored speech_act_id; the world authoritatively validates fresh state. An accepted utterance is echoed, may observe one bounded reply, and leaves later speech delivery in pushes. A prompt-bound answer (args_json.semantic_context), or an utterance on an action that carries an authored input form (a name or text field), also returns the next open prompt row as receipt.next_prompt, waited for inside the same reply window plus a short grace after the reply, so the next answer needs no manipulation_context read; next_prompt.status says whether a row opened, was already open, or timed out. An action's input.fields[].channel (from spellkave_manipulation_context) says how a field travels: "utterance" fields are read from what you say (plain text for one field, a JSON object keyed by field name for several); sending them in args_json is refused as utterance_required before dispatch.

target_id.description: Typed target reference to communicate with — use an observed participant or location reference (e.g. 'entity:42'). The world authoritatively validates the attempt; a bare numeric id is ambiguous and may be rejected or misresolved.

utterance.description: Optional words to say. On acceptance they are delivered to the world as dispatch_text, echoed in the receipt, and may open the bounded reply window.

args_json.description: Optional JSON argument blob, passed 1:1 to the world. Defaults to '{}'. A prompt-bound answer (a speech_act_id listed in a prompts[] row's responseActionIds in spellkave_manipulation_context, e.g. dm/dialog/choice/2) must carry that prompts[] row here as {"semantic_context": <row>}; without it the world rejects the answer with prompt_context_required.

tools.name: spellkave_end_turn
tools.label: Spellkave End Turn
tools.description: End the connected actor's current turn in the in-world turn/scene (not the MCP connection), without supplying a session id. The world resolves active participation and rejects no-session/off-turn calls (`no_session` still allows exploration; or it is not your turn). NOTE: advancing the turn does NOT refresh the new current actor's available actions — only turn-gated (action-economy) rows are recomputed on a turn boundary; other available actions stay whatever they were. Movement is unaffected either way: spellkave_scene's exits are always current, so they are never stale from a missed refresh. On dispatch, the result carries `receipt` (what the world did) and a sibling `observation` (a fixed 'Your turn ends.' line on success, or 'Nothing happens.' on rejection). On a successful advance, the receipt also carries the NEW in-world `session` block (`in_session`/`current_actor`/`my_turn`) — whose turn it is next in that scene, not the MCP connection.

tools.name: spellkave_manipulate
tools.label: Spellkave Manipulate
tools.description: Attempt one authored action against one typed target. Prefer action_id and target_id from spellkave_manipulation_context when it is ready; those facts support composition but never promise success. Direct typed attempts remain allowed and the world authoritatively validates fresh state. Args pass 1:1 and success is provenance-observed. For a prompt-bound dialog answer (a prompts[] row, dm/dialog/choice/N) or any free-text creation field use spellkave_communicate instead: it carries the utterance and returns the next open prompt row on its receipt; this tool does not. A field whose input.fields[].channel is "utterance" cannot be sent here: the attempt is refused as utterance_required and names the spellkave_communicate speech act to use.

target_id.description: Typed target reference to manipulate — prefer target_ref from spellkave_manipulation_context (e.g. 'entity:42', 'item:7'). A bare numeric id is ambiguous and may misresolve a contained item.

action_id.description: Action identifier to attempt against the target.

args_json.description: Optional JSON argument blob, passed 1:1 to r_manipulate. Defaults to '{}'. A prompt-bound action (an action_id listed in a prompts[] row's responseActionIds in spellkave_manipulation_context) must carry that prompts[] row here as {"semantic_context": <row>}; without it the world rejects the attempt with prompt_context_required.

argumentGates: Select an eligible caller-owned binding when multiple presences can perform this act; server checks target extent and consent for as_body_id.

tools.name: spellkave_docs
tools.label: Modding Docs
tools.description: Orient on the packaged authoring corpus (DOCS-ONLY). Index (`shape: "index"`): id/title/kind/summary/has_example. Query (`shape: "hits"`): ranked summary+excerpt only (not full bodies). Doc (`shape: "doc"`): one id — oversized docs default to outline (headings); pass `section` for one heading or `full` for the entire body. Narrow hits with `doc_paths`; `limit` default 3. Reads ONLY the packaged corpus.

query.description: Free-text question about how to author something, e.g. 'how do I express object decay over time'. Matched (keyword/heading) against the packaged authoring corpus. Omit to list the bounded corpus index instead of querying it.

doc.description: Exact corpus id (a `rel` from the index or a hit, e.g. 'dm-oversight') — returns that ONE doc whole: its prose body, the worked-example walkthrough when the id has both halves, and the complete example manifest TOML when `has_example` is true. This is how you get something copyable rather than only readable. Mutually exclusive with `query`; takes precedence if both are set.

section.description: Optional heading text or anchor within `doc` — returns only that section's markdown instead of the full body. Unknown section fails (does not silently return the whole doc). Ignored without `doc`.

outline.description: With `doc`, return title + summary + heading list only (no full body). Default for oversized docs when neither `section` nor `full` is set.

full.description: With `doc`, force the complete body even when oversized (tool-reference, long references). Prefer `section` instead. Default false.

doc_paths.description: Optional corpus-id filter (substring match) restricting the search to specific packaged docs. Only applies with `query` set; can only narrow the corpus, never widen it.

limit.description: Max number of doc slices to return when `query` is set (default 3).

promptGuidelines: Use spellkave_docs to pull the smallest relevant authoring-doc slice before guessing a manifest row or DSL form.

tools.name: spellkave_query
tools.label: Query Manifest / Definitions
tools.description: Read the authored world — merges the former spellkave_manifest_inspect + spellkave_lookup, plus the #1968 definition-lookup gap's missing single-row detail/ref-traversal capability, into ONE tool. Dispatch is inferred from which fields you pass (no mode flag): omit `kind` for a workspace/target summary (bundle ids + row-kind -> count map); pass `kind` alone (or with `pattern`) for a bounded catalog list (default ids-only; add fields:'preferred' or fields:[col,…] to project extra scalars — e.g. entities preferred yields name+place_node_id for who-is-where in one call); pass `kind` + `id` for the complete authored row, its source, and (by default) its outbound/inbound refs — chase a ref by re-calling this tool with its own {kind, id} (e.g. a capability -> its affordance_templates -> their action_definitions -> outcome_templates). Sources, in order: the workspace scratch manifest, plus the active connection-level `target` when wired, or the legacy live `context.db` when no target is configured (result.source says which). Offline with neither, this is workspace-only. `target` overrides the source for THIS call only (read-only — write verbs offer no such override).

kind.description: A manifest row-kind name (a ROW_KIND_NATURAL_KEY key — e.g. 'capability_definitions', 'affordance_templates', 'action_definitions', 'outcome_templates', 'entity_definitions', 'area_shape_definitions', 'resource_definitions'), the SAME vocabulary spellkave_write_rows and every define_* verb already use — not a closed enum. Also accepts a `*_tag` satellite kind (e.g. 'resource_definition_tag', 'capability_definition_tag') — these have a TWO-field composite key (parent id + tag) instead of a single natural key; see `schema: true` for the field order. Omit for a workspace/target summary (bundle ids + a row-kind -> count map) instead of listing one kind.

id.description: An exact natural-key value within `kind` — returns the complete authored row (detail shape), its source, and (by default) its refs. For a composite-keyed `*_tag` satellite kind, this is its ordered key fields' values joined by '::' (e.g. 'srd/wis::ability_score' for resource_definition_tag's `{resource_definition_id, tag}` — get the exact ids from a `kind`-only list call first). Mutually exclusive with `pattern`; requires `kind`.

pattern.description: A substring filter on `kind`'s ids (its natural-key value, or its '::'-joined composite-key value for a `*_tag` satellite kind) — returns a filtered list instead of the full catalog. Mutually exclusive with `id`; requires `kind`.

bundle.description: Restrict to rows stamped with this bundle_id (summary/list shapes only).

fields.description: List shape only (`kind` without `id`; ignored for detail/summary/schema). Default (omit): token-safe catalog — each item is only `{ id, bundle_id? }`. `preferred`: project a small kind-specific field set (e.g. entities → name, place_node_id, kind, entity_def_id) so one list call can answer who-is-where without N detail round-trips. Explicit string[]: project exactly those column names from each row (unknown/missing names omitted; nested values skipped). `id` is always present; `bundle_id` is included when the row has it.

refs.description: Detail shape only (`kind`+`id`; ignored otherwise). 'outbound': fields on this row pointing elsewhere (already-computed string-ref heuristic). 'both' additionally computes inbound_refs — every OTHER row anywhere in the resolved source whose own outbound ref points AT this row, grouped by referencing kind — so a caller traverses a chain (e.g. capability -> affordance -> action -> outcome) by re-calling spellkave_query with a ref's own {kind, id}, no separate traversal tool needed. Default: 'both' when `id` is set.

target.description: #1968 connection-level target override (READ-only — no write verb offers this): 'workspace' reads ONLY the workspace scratch manifest, ignoring any connection-level target/live db this call would otherwise consult. 'local' reads ONLY the active local folder target — errors if none is configured. 'live' reads ONLY the active live target (or the legacy live db when no target is wired at all) — errors if neither is available. Omit for the default union: workspace + whatever is configured (result.source says which).

schema.description: Ask what a row of `kind` may CONTAIN instead of which rows exist (#1983): with `kind`, that row kind's required fields, field types, and natural/composite key; without `kind`, the row-kind vocabulary itself (every kind the manifest schema defines, flagged for whether this tool can also list its rows). Schema covers all 79 manifest row kinds — a superset of the ~53 `id`/`pattern` can address: the 40 with a single-column natural key, plus the `*_tag` satellite kinds and `tag_capability_grant` with a two-field composite key (finding #9; sk-bwd). Ignores `id`/`pattern`/`bundle`/`target`: a row kind's shape is the same everywhere, so no source is consulted.

tools.promptSnippet: Inspect authored/live rows and definitions by kind and id, or list what exists
promptGuidelines: Use spellkave_query before spellkave_write_rows or a define_* verb to confirm an id doesn't already exist, or to check whether a referenced niche_id/capability_id/entity_def is already authored.
Call spellkave_query with kind+id to fetch one row's full detail and inbound/outbound references — chase a reference by re-calling spellkave_query with the ref's own {kind, id}.

Place graph + who-is-where: spellkave_map_graph, then spellkave_query kind=entities fields=preferred (group by place_node_id). Default list is ids-only — request fields when you need columns. Deeper playbook: spellkave_docs doc=place-graph-occupancy (only if needed).

tools.name: spellkave_eval
tools.label: Evaluate DSL Expression
tools.description: Evaluate a Spellkave DSL expression offline using the wasm-compiled resolution evaluator. Accepts expression source, kind (predicate, int, or text), author-supplied facts grouped by subject or pool, and die faces in draw order. Returns the result value with its type, draws used, and evaluation trace, or a named rejection naming the cause.

expression.description: DSL source text to evaluate offline.

facts.description: The values the expression reads, grouped by subject (actor, target, location, session, world, actor.wielded_item, equipped items, bindings, event), plus roll_tables, item_sources, roll_modifier_bias, event_kind, occupants_at, peers_near_target, channel_pools. Validated strictly in Rust.

dice.description: Die faces in draw order consumed by stochastic roll operators and roll tables.

tools.promptSnippet: Evaluate a DSL expression offline with traced execution and fixed dice
promptGuidelines: spellkave_eval: evaluate offline; no running node or connection needed.
spellkave_eval: false predicate returns ok=true with value={type:'Bool', value:false}; check errors and bounds reject with ok=false.

tools.name: spellkave_map_graph
tools.label: Map Graph
tools.description: Render the authored place-graph as the shared spatial-graph view. Sources rows only through the same workspace/target/live resolution as spellkave_query (place_graphs, place_nodes, place_edges, actor_spatial_locations). output_type picks the ONE artifact computed and returned: 'svg' (default) — this tool's picture-first interactive use case: the raw SVG in details.svg plus an ImageContent PNG for hosts that render tool images (Pi TUI / Ghostty Kitty). 'utf8'/'ascii'/'braille' return that text variant in the like-named details field instead (no image). 'inventory' skips the graph picture entirely, details.inventory only. 'jpg' writes a backdrop-composed JPEG to output_dir/output_name and returns its path as details.jpg_path — no svg/ascii/utf8/braille text in the response.

graph.description: Optional place_graph_id filter — when set, draw that graph (any substrate). Omit to compose every outdoor positioned graph (world map).

slice.description: How to project multi-floor / unpositioned graphs: elevation_band (one floor), all_floors_offset (floors side-by-side), topology_only (adjacency layout), metric (all z in one plane), h3_world (outdoor multi-graph from cell_res10 — same plane idea as web WorldMapView). Omit for auto (indoor multi-z → elevation_band at z=0; outdoor compose uses h3 when cells present).

z_tolerance.description: Half-width of elevation_band in elevation units (default 0.5).

lod.description: structure = rooms/routes only (no occupancy badges); furnished = + actor counts (default).

output_type.description: Which single artifact to render — the engine computes ONLY this one (bead sk-due: the old `terminal` param picked the text body while the engine rendered svg + utf8 + ascii + braille + inventory regardless, every call). 'svg' (default) — this tool's own interactive picture-first use case: the raw SVG in details.svg plus an ImageContent PNG for hosts that render tool images (Pi TUI / Ghostty Kitty). 'utf8'/'ascii'/'braille' return that text variant in the like-named details field instead (no image). 'inventory' skips the graph picture entirely, details.inventory only. 'jpg' writes a backdrop-composed JPEG to output_dir/output_name and returns its path as details.jpg_path — no svg/ascii/utf8/braille text in the response.

output_dir.description: output_type='jpg' only; ignored otherwise. Directory to write the map-art JPEG into — absolute, or RELATIVE to the host process's own cwd. Optional: omit for a fresh temp directory (mkdtemp). Resolves this graph's authored [[map_layers]] backdrop (unmasked — same drawn-in-full contract every backdrop render in this package follows), rasterizes via resvg then encodes via ffmpeg -q:v 4, skipping the rewrite when an unchanged render already sits there (deterministic churn guard).

output_name.description: output_type='jpg' only; ignored otherwise. Base filename (no extension) for the JPEG written under output_dir. Optional: omit for a name derived from graph, or 'map' when graph itself is also omitted (a world-compose call).

target.description: Same read-only source override as spellkave_query (`workspace` | `local` | `live`). Omit for the default workspace+configured-target union.

tools.promptSnippet: Draw the place-graph from existing query sources
promptGuidelines: Prefer spellkave_map_graph when you need a picture of place connectivity; badges are occupancy counts only.
Indoor/multi-floor: pass graph= and slice=elevation_band with z= (default auto z=0), or slice=all_floors_offset for side-by-side floors; topology_only when nodes lack positions.

Place graph + people: after spellkave_map_graph, call spellkave_query kind=entities fields=preferred and group by place_node_id (usually two calls). Optional third: place_nodes fields=preferred for labels.

Pass graph=<place_graph_id> to draw one graph; omit to compose every outdoor positioned graph (H3 plane when cell_res10 present). Deeper playbook only if needed: spellkave_docs doc=place-graph-occupancy.
Outdoor world: omit graph (or slice=h3_world) so CLI/agent map_graph matches web outdoor H3 placement methodology.
output_type=jpg to save a map-art file instead of an inline picture; utf8/ascii/braille/inventory are cheaper text-only reads when you don't need a picture at all.

tools.name: spellkave_declare_inexpressible
tools.label: Declare Inexpressible
tools.description: Declare that no documented row kind / DSL form can express this intent within the validator's surface — a runtime/schema gap surfaced through authoring. A well-justified 'I cannot express this' is a SUCCESSFUL finding, not a failure.

reason.description: Precisely why no documented row kind / DSL form can express this intent within the validator's surface.

tools.name: spellkave_note_doc_gap
tools.label: Note Doc Gap
tools.description: Record a discrepancy between what the modding docs implied and what the validator actually accepted. Does NOT end your run — keep authoring. Sharpens the docs shipped to other authors.

doc.description: Which corpus doc id you were working from, e.g. 'dsl-grammar'.

expected.description: What the doc led you to expect.

actual.description: What the validator actually did — the discrepancy.

tools.name: spellkave_author_place
tools.label: Author Place (verb PoC)
tools.description: PoC (#1968): author ONE place_graph + its place_nodes (+ optional place_edges) in a single call, wrapping the existing patchManifest place ops. Self-scaffolds the `[[bundles]]` header if `bundle` has none yet (FIX②b). Nodes get metric positions (explicit x/y or auto circle/line) and optional elevation. substrate defaults to outdoor; pass substrate:'indoor' for buildings. PoC boundary: one place_graph per call. map_graph draws outdoor world-compose by default; pass graph=<id> to draw an indoor plan. Top-level `description` sets the GRAPH's own description; each `nodes[].description` sets that ONE node's own arrival prose instead (T5 follow-up) — author both when a node deserves its own sensory detail beyond the graph-level blurb.

bundle.description: bundle_id stamped on every generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (#1968 smart default).

substrate.description: substrate_id for the graph and every node (core: outdoor | indoor | tactical). Default 'outdoor'. Houses/interiors should use 'indoor'.

parent_graph_id.description: Composition parent place_graph_id (ADR-0029 / Item 25). Empty/omit = root. Nested outdoor graphs project into the parent frame on the world map.

origin_cell_res10.description: Root outdoor H3 res10 anchor as decimal u64 string. Only composition roots should set this; res7/res4 parents are derived. Nested graphs omit (origin stays 0).

bearing.description: Clockwise rotation degrees relative to parent/world frame (ADR-0029). Default 0.

metres_per_unit.description: Graph unit → metres (ADR-0029). Default 1. Outdoor world maps often use >1.

display_name.description: place_graph display_name; default title-cased graph local id.

id.description: Fully-qualified place-node id '<place_graph_id>/<local_id>' (e.g. 'aoe_blast/arena/center'). PoC boundary: bare local ids are not supported.

name.description: display_name; defaults to a title-cased local id.

x.description: Optional metric graph-local pos_x (integer graph units). When any node omits x/y, author_place auto-layouts all nodes on a circle (n>=3) or a line (n=1..2).

y.description: Optional metric graph-local pos_y (integer graph units). See `x`.

elevation.description: Optional graph-local pose_elevation (metres-ish via graph metres_per_unit). Use for floors/cellars (e.g. 0 ground, -3 cellar). Omit for 0 with pose_elevation_present=true.

cell_res10.description: Optional outdoor H3 res10 cell as decimal u64 string (parents res7/res4 derived via h3-js). Prefer strings so values above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER stay exact.

description.description: Sets THIS node's own `place_nodes.description` column (T5 follow-up, #1968 pattern: a first-class field, never a metadata_attachments detour — same shape as the top-level `description` param below, which sets the GRAPH's own description instead). Read by movement-observation tools (e.g. spellkave_move) as the arrival prose for THIS node; falls back to the graph's own description only on a graph-crossing move when omitted.

extent_shape_id.description: place_nodes.extent_shape_id (place-node-extent D-2, sk-71u): an explicit spatial extent for THIS node — one of the KNOWN_AREA_SHAPE_IDS kernel shapes (e.g. 'core/area/sphere', 'core/area/cube'). Overrides the bundle's own default_extent_shape_id (spellkave_define_bundle) for this node only. Pair with `extent_params_json`; omit both to fall back to the bundle default.

extent_params_json.description: place_nodes.extent_params_json — the params_json paired with `extent_shape_id` (e.g. '{"radius_m": 2.5}' for core/area/sphere). Only meaningful alongside `extent_shape_id`.

nodes.description: One or more place nodes. Every id must share ONE common parent path (one place_graph per call — a PoC boundary); the FIRST node becomes the place_graph's anchor_node_id.

edges.description: [from_node_id, to_node_id] pairs; both ends must be in `nodes`. Pass [] for disconnected nodes (e.g. two same-radius cells with no traversal edge between them, as the worked example does).

description.description: Sets the generated place_graph's own `description` column (#1968 — a first-class, never load-bearing authoring field, not a metadata_attachments row).

tools.promptSnippet: Author one place_graph with nodes and edges (outdoor or indoor)
promptGuidelines: Use spellkave_author_place for topology (nodes+edges); pass nodes[].x/y for layout or omit for auto circle; nodes[].elevation for floors.
Houses/interiors: substrate:'indoor'. Outdoor regions: omit or substrate:'outdoor'.
Author nodes[].description for a node's own 1-2 sentence arrival prose; it wins over the graph-level description on that node's own moves.
After authoring, spellkave_map_graph shows the picture (pass graph= for indoor); for live worlds call spellkave_apply_manifest_delta with no args to commit the scratch.
Deeper spatial playbook: spellkave_docs doc=place-graph-occupancy (read path) or spatial-minimal-cell (row shape).

tools.name: spellkave_link_places
tools.label: Link Places
tools.description: Author a portal between two existing place_nodes (same graph or cross-graph). Writes place_edges with place_graph_id "" when graphs differ (Stonehill pattern), sets substrate_crossing automatically for outdoor↔indoor. Does NOT attach a place_edge_affordance by default (ADR-0101): an ordinary edge just inherits the bundle/graph movement_default (spellkave_set_movement_default) via place_edges.inherit_movement_default, which defaults to true — zero per-edge rows for ordinary walking. Pass portal:true (+ affordance_template_id / bindings_json) only for a special affordance you want attached to THIS edge at creation time; spellkave_bind_edge_affordance is the preferred (FK-validated) path for that, including after the edge already exists. Use after spellkave_author_place on both sides.

bundle.description: bundle_id stamped on generated edges. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle`.

from.description: Fully-qualified place_node id (must already exist in workspace/target).

to.description: Fully-qualified place_node id (must already exist in workspace/target).

substrate_crossing.description: Force substrate_crossing. Omit to auto: true when the two nodes' substrates differ, or when they belong to different place_graphs (cross-graph portal).

portal.description: Attach a place_edge_affordance on each edge (default FALSE, ADR-0101 — ordinary edges inherit the bundle/graph movement_default instead, no per-edge row needed).
