Re-running with the SAME entity_key upserts its owned rows, same as `key_prefix`. Mutually exclusive with `key_prefix`; only legal for a single instance — omit `count` or set it to 1.

name.description: sk-ntz.1: THIS placement's own explicit, VERBATIM `entities.name`/`actors.name` override — used AS-IS on every instance in THIS placement, no ordinal suffix appended (contrast the default title-cased `kind`/`entity_def` naming, which DOES append an ordinal for multi-instance placements). Overrides the flat `name` when both are set (THIS placement's own `name` wins) — the escape hatch that let raw write_rows chains author a custom display name this verb previously could not reproduce (the fold this verb was widened for, sk-ntz.1, otherwise had no way to keep a fixture's own 'Fast-lane Hero' style name). Mutually exclusive with `name_prefix`. Omit for the existing default: title-cased `kind`/`entity_def`, ordinal-suffixed for multi-instance placements — unchanged.

name_prefix.description: sk-jay0.7.15.3: THIS placement's own display-name STEM — replaces only the title-cased `kind`/`entity_def` half of the derived name and KEEPS the ordinal (`'<name_prefix> <n>'`). The group-placement counterpart to verbatim `name` (which is used AS-IS with no ordinal, so a count>1 batch would otherwise share one identical name). Overrides the flat `name_prefix` when both are set (THIS placement's own `name_prefix` wins). Mutually exclusive with `name`. Illegal with `entity_key` (no ordinal is minted — use `name` for a single literal key). Omit for the existing default — unchanged.

quantity.description: sk-ntz.1: THIS placement's own explicit `entities.quantity` (stack size) override for every instance in THIS placement — spellkave_place_entity ONLY (a stackable item's own on-instance count, e.g. a 10-credit purse); spellkave_place_actor rejects a set `quantity` outright (actors carry no stack — use spellkave_place_entity instead). Overrides the flat `quantity` when both are set (THIS placement's own `quantity` wins). Omit for the schema default (1) — unchanged.

tags.description: One INSTANCE-level entity_tag row per tag ('this goblin is the leader / faction X') — NOT an entity_definition_tag. Tag-grammar membership (MF-VAL-300) and dedup are enforced by the shared validator at commit; an unknown-grammar tag is reported as a diagnostic, not persisted. When a tag has authored tag_capability_grant rows (workspace/live), the result surfaces 'tag X grants capability Y' so the author sees the consequence — informational, never blocking.

placements.description: MULTI-LOCATION shape (FIX①, #1968): one or more {at, count?, resources?, tags?} groups placing the SAME kind/entity_def split across DIFFERENT place_nodes in a single call (e.g. 3 targets at the blast center + 1 bystander at the fringe). Mutually exclusive with the flat `at`/`count`/`resources`/`tags` — set ONE shape or the other, never both.

description.description: Sets EVERY placed entity's own `description` column (across every placement) — e.g. 'the guard with the limp' (#1968 — a first-class, never load-bearing authoring field, not a metadata_attachments row).

key_prefix.description: FLAT shape only (mutually exclusive with `placements` — set `placements[].key_prefix` there instead). #1968 workspace idempotency: see `placements[].key_prefix`'s description for the full semantics — this is the same field, for the single-location flat shape. Mutually exclusive with `entity_key`.

entity_key.description: FLAT shape only (mutually exclusive with `placements` — set `placements[].entity_key` there instead). sk-9ll.6: see `placements[].entity_key`'s description for the full semantics — this is the same field, for the single-location flat shape.

name.description: sk-ntz.1: FLAT shape (also `placements[].name`, which wins when both are set): sets EVERY placed entity's own `entities.name`/`actors.name` verbatim (no ordinal suffix), instead of the default title-cased `kind`/`entity_def` naming. A first-class, never load-bearing authoring field, mirrors `description`'s own shared-across-every-placement convention. Mutually exclusive with `name_prefix`. Omit for the existing default — unchanged.

name_prefix.description: sk-jay0.7.15.3: FLAT shape (also `placements[].name_prefix`, which wins when both are set): replaces only the title-cased `kind`/`entity_def` half of the derived name and KEEPS the ordinal (`'<name_prefix> <n>'`) across every placed instance. The group-placement counterpart to verbatim `name`. Mutually exclusive with `name`. Illegal with `entity_key`. Omit for the existing default — unchanged.

quantity.description: sk-ntz.1: FLAT shape (also `placements[].quantity`, which wins when both are set): sets EVERY placed entity's own `entities.quantity` (stack size) — spellkave_place_entity ONLY; spellkave_place_actor rejects a set `quantity` (actors carry no stack — use spellkave_place_entity for a stackable item instance instead). Omit for the schema default (1) — unchanged.

tools.name: spellkave_bind_actor
tools.label: Bind Actor (verb)
tools.description: #1968 verb-UX round 6: bind an already-placed actor's identity (actor_identities, upsert-by-entity_key) and, optionally, grant it one or more capabilities (actor_capabilities) in a single call — folds the genesis-window self-grant idiom (an identity bind + a `frontier.apply_manifest` grant, the `srd/regdar`/`phandelver/hero` pattern every ad-hoc live-authored actor bundle needs post-core/player-retirement) from 2 spellkave_write_rows calls into 1. `entity_key` must already carry an actor_spatial_locations row (workspace, live, or the active target) — place it first via spellkave_place_actor (mirrors spellkave_define_behavior's own `grant_to` precondition). #1968 workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME entity_key's identity bind REPLACES it (never duplicates — the server itself upserts on (actor_id, identity), and every corpus fixture binds one entity_key to exactly one identity); each capabilities[] grant upserts by (actor_entity_key, capability_id, source), mirroring add-capability-grant.

bundle.description: bundle_id stamped on every generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (#1968 smart default).

entity_key.description: entity_key of an already-placed actor (e.g. via spellkave_place_actor) — must already carry an actor_spatial_locations row (workspace, live, or the active target); this call does not place one.

identity.description: actor_identities.identity. Default '$sender' resolves to whoever submits the applying delta. Pass a concrete identity hex string only when binding to a KNOWN, fixed identity instead.

role.description: actor_identities.role. Default 'primary' (the corpus-dominant value; 'dm' is the one observed override). NOT a cosmetic label: r_claim_actor refuses every value but 'primary', so authoring 'dm' deliberately makes the seat un-self-claimable — right for a human DM anchor handed over by the operator, wrong for a programmatic seat that wants the self-claim path. It never affects visibility or write authority, which come from the capability grant alone.

capability_id.description: actor_capabilities.capability_id — must already resolve to an authored capability_definitions row (workspace, live, or the active target); this call does not auto-create it. The genesis-window self-grant idiom passes 'frontier.apply_manifest' (a bootstrap-seeded core capability).

source.description: actor_capabilities.source. Omit for the schema default 'manifest' (mirrors `add-capability-grant`'s own default). The genesis-window self-grant idiom passes 'core' — the GRANTED capability's owning bundle (frontier.apply_manifest lives in core), not the granted actor's own entity_key.

capabilities.description: actor_capabilities grants issued to the SAME entity_key, alongside the identity bind. Default `[]` (identity-only bind — no grant). Ordinary capability rows are supported; frontier.* capability requests are refused with a pointer to spellkave_grant_role.

tools.name: spellkave_tag_entity
tools.label: Tag Entity (verb)
tools.description: sk-ntz.2: retag an already-placed entity's INSTANCE-level entity_tag rows from a call/file OTHER than the one that placed it (e.g. crypt-fight.ts tagging a hero placed by hero.ts) — the narrow post-placement counterpart to spellkave_place_entity/spellkave_place_actor's own `tags` param, for exactly the case those verbs cannot cover: an entity_key placed elsewhere. `entity_key` must already carry an entities row (workspace or the active target) — place it first via spellkave_place_entity/spellkave_place_actor (mirrors spellkave_bind_actor's own precondition). Default `mode: 'add'` upserts the listed tags and leaves every OTHER tag on the entity untouched (idempotent); `mode: 'replace'` clears every existing entity_tag row for `entity_key` first, then reseeds exactly `tags` — use `replace` only when THIS call owns the entity's complete tag set, since it WOULD clobber tags authored by the entity's own placement call otherwise. Tag-grammar membership (MF-VAL-300) is enforced by the shared validator at commit, not re-validated here; when a tag carries an authored tag_capability_grant, the result's `tag_capability_grants` reports the capability it live-grants (informational, never blocking).

bundle.description: bundle_id stamped on every generated entity_tag row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (#1968 smart default). NOTE: this is the bundle OWNING the new tag row(s), not necessarily the bundle that placed `entity_key` — a cross-bundle caller stamps ITS own bundle_id here (the kavemouth idiom this verb replaces: crypt-fight.ts/dm-npc.ts tag the hero placed in hero.ts, all three sharing one bundle in that fixture, but nothing requires it).

entity_key.description: entity_key of an already-placed entity (e.g. via spellkave_place_entity/spellkave_place_actor, in THIS bundle or another) — must already carry an entities row (workspace or the active target); this call does not place one. Use this verb instead of re-invoking the placement tool when the entity's placement call lives in a DIFFERENT file/call than the one adding this tag.

tags.description: One INSTANCE-level entity_tag row per tag, mirroring spellkave_place_entity/spellkave_place_actor's own `tags` param exactly (same row shape, same MF-VAL-300 grammar, same tag_capability_grant diagnostic) — the difference is WHEN: this verb runs AFTER the entity already exists, against an entity_key placed by a DIFFERENT call/file.

mode.description: Default 'add': upsert the listed tags, leaving every OTHER tag already on this entity_key untouched (idempotent — re-listing an already-present tag is a no-op) — the safe default for a cross-file caller that does not own the entity's full tag set (this verb's whole reason to exist: REPLACING would clobber tags the entity's OWN placement call already authored elsewhere). Set 'replace' only when THIS call owns the entity's complete tag set: it clears EVERY existing entity_tag row for `entity_key` first, then reseeds exactly `tags` (a re-run with fewer tags drops the stale ones, mirroring spellkave_place_entity/spellkave_place_actor's own clear-and-reseed).

tools.name: spellkave_equip_item
tools.label: Equip Item (verb)
tools.description: sk-9ll.3: equip an already-placed, already-stowed item into a named equipment slot on an actor (actor_equipment_slots, upsert-by-(actor_entity_key, slot_id)) — folds the 'give the hero a starter weapon' idiom's raw actor_equipment_slots write into one checked call. `slot_id` existence and `item_entity_key`'s existence/placeability are enforced by the SAME validator the linter and manifest admission use (no bespoke re-check here); THIS call's own precondition is the one thing only it can see across separate tool calls — a slot already occupied by a DIFFERENT item is a hard rejection (matches the runtime EquipItem affordance's SlotAlreadyOccupied check), while re-equipping the SAME item into the SAME slot is idempotent.

bundle.description: bundle_id stamped on the generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (#1968 smart default).

actor_entity_key.description: actor_equipment_slots.actor_entity_key — must already carry an actor_spatial_locations row (workspace, live, or the active target); place it first via spellkave_place_actor.

item_entity_key.description: actor_equipment_slots.item_key — an already-authored entities row that entity_containment already places inside actor_entity_key (stow it first via spellkave_stow_item).

slot_id.description: actor_equipment_slots.slot_id — must already resolve to an authored equipment_slot_definitions row.

tools.name: spellkave_stow_item
tools.label: Stow Item (verb)
tools.description: sk-9ll.3: place an already-authored entity inside a container (entity_containment, upsert-by-entity_key — a re-authored containment MOVES the entity, mirroring add-entity-containment's own upsert semantics). Folds the 'starter pack straight into the hero' / 'item straight onto its holder' idiom (container_entity_key omitted, defaults to actor_entity_key) AND the nested-container idiom (container_entity_key explicit, e.g. a torch into an already-stowed field kit) into one checked call, replacing a raw spellkave_write_rows entity_containment call.

bundle.description: bundle_id stamped on the generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (#1968 smart default).

actor_entity_key.description: The actor stowing item_entity_key — must already carry an actor_spatial_locations row (workspace, live, or the active target); place it first via spellkave_place_actor. Also the DEFAULT container when container_entity_key is omitted.

item_entity_key.description: entity_containment.entity_key — an already-placed entity (workspace or the active target) to move into container_entity_key (or actor_entity_key when container_entity_key is omitted).

container_entity_key.description: entity_containment.container_entity_key. Default actor_entity_key — the common 'give the actor this item directly' case (a starter weapon straight into the hero's inventory). Pass a DIFFERENT already-placed container (e.g. a field kit already stowed on the actor) to nest item_entity_key inside IT instead (the torch-inside-the-field-kit idiom).

slot_id.description: entity_containment.slot_id — machine-port slot id. Default '' (loose carriage — the common item-in-backpack/actor-holding-item case, not a machine port).

tools.name: spellkave_define_behavior
tools.label: Define Behavior (verb PoC)
tools.description: PoC (#1968): author ONE capability→affordance→action→outcome→consequence→frame_write chain (+ an optional cost debit) in a single call, granted to `grant_to`. Drives @spellkave/world-author's `clusterRows` — the SAME behavior-cluster builder the SRD content drivers use (FIX③, #1968 de-fork) — bundle-namespaced via `BehaviorConfig.idNamespace`. `primitive` fields are CLOSED PoC enums — only the real kernel shapes the worked fireball/find_familiar/core-mark examples need are wired; anything else fails loudly naming the PoC boundary. #1968 US9 VERB EXPANSION: `effect.write.primitive` now also accepts 'Spawn' (Brief 26 EffectPrimitive::Spawn — instantiate an entity_def at the actor's own node) and 'Inscribe' (the raw FrameWriteOp::Inscribe trace idiom — a durable typed footprint, no resource delta); both require `offered_when.target: 'self'|'place'` (a target concept beyond 'hit others in a radius') and never combine with `effect.shape`/`effect.per_target_gate`. `target: 'self'` needs a `cost` (else this tool errors BEFORE validation with a hint, MF-VAL-263); `target: 'place'` needs none (self_eligible stays false, so the self-budget check never engages). `effect.write.resource` (ModifyResource) / `effect.write.entity_def` (Spawn) must already be authored (this PoC never auto-creates write-target resources/blueprints — use spellkave_define_resource / spellkave_define_entity_type first); `cost.pool`, if new, IS auto-created with generic bounds. #1968 workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES the whole generated cluster (capability/ outcome/affordance/action/consequence/frame-write/live-wiring rows) rather than duplicating it.

bundle.description: bundle_id stamped on every generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (#1968 smart default).

id.description: Behavior key stem — derives capability_id '<bundle>/spell/<id>' and action_id '<bundle>/cast_<id>' (+ its outcome/affordance/consequence siblings), unless overridden by `capability_id`.

capability_id.description: #1968 verb-UX round 2: override the derived '<bundle>/spell/<id>' capability_id — e.g. for a CATALOG spell whose entity_definitions.entity_def_id already exists under a different id shape (mirrors compose.ts's ActorBehavior.capabilityId — for a catalog spell this MUST equal the catalog entity_def_id so the capability IS the catalog identity, #835). `action_id` is never touched by this — only the capability's own id changes.

action_prefix.description: #1968 srd-migration round: override the derived action id's prefix — the full action id is '<bundle>/<action_prefix><id>' (default 'cast_', e.g. id='fireball' -> '<bundle>/cast_fireball'). Pass '' to derive a BARE '<bundle>/<id>' action id (e.g. the Hex/Bless/Bardic-Inspiration condition-modified-roll family's WRITER/CONSUMER pair, whose action ids are '<bundle>/<key>', not '<bundle>/cast_<key>') — mirrors compose.ts's BehaviorConfig.actionPrefix verbatim; outcome/affordance/success ids all derive from the SAME action id, so this affects all four.

emit_capability.description: #1968 srd-migration round: whether this call authors a capability_definitions row for `capability_id`/the derived id. Default true. Pass false when the capability ALREADY exists (authored by ANOTHER call/fragment, e.g. a feat grant that already created it) and this call should REUSE it — `required_capability`/`actor_capabilities`/the niche all still key on `capability_id` (which then MUST be set — omitting it AND setting false derives an id no prior call could have authored), but no duplicate capability_definitions row is emitted (mirrors compose.ts's ActorBehavior.emitCapability, a required field there, made an optional smart default here since every prior verb caller wanted true).

display_name.description: #1968 verb-UX round 2: overrides the derived 'Cast <TitleCase id>' display name stamped onto every generated row that carries one (capability/action/affordance/outcome). Omit for the smart default — naive per-word title-casing mangles a multi-word id containing a preposition (e.g. 'circle_of_death' -> 'Cast Circle Of Death' instead of 'Cast Circle of Death').

description.description: Sets the generated capability_definitions row's own `description` column (#1968) — the capability is this behavior's natural authoring-identity anchor, so that is where the description lands (NOT the affordance/action/outcome/consequence/resource rows this verb also generates).

observation.description: #1968 B-9: authored PLAYER-facing prose for what a player perceives on a successful manipulate or sensing outcome — distinct from `description` above, which stays operator-only on capability_definitions. Sets the generated outcome_templates row's own `description` column (its actual authoring/read home — see outcome_template.rs's doc comment for why that table, not action_definitions/consequence_templates). May reference ONLY the frozen placeholders `{target_name}`, `{actor_name}`, `{place_name}` (resolved from data the player already sees, never a raw id) — a state-dereferencing value (HP, a resource, a condition) belongs in the DSL outcome expression, not here, and an unknown placeholder or a description over 500 chars is rejected at validation. Omit for the existing default: the tool result carries an honest `observation: null` + `observation_gap`, byte-identical to today.

tags.description: #1968 verb-UX round 2: the FULL capability_definition_tag AND action_definition_tag row set — when set, REPLACES the single `action_class` tag as the authoritative list for BOTH satellites (include `action_class`'s own value in `tags` too, if wanted — it is not auto-prepended). Omit for the legacy default: `action_class` alone becomes the one action tag, no capability tags — `action_class` itself is REQUIRED either way (no default of its own, #1968 finding A1): this param only controls what ELSE joins it, never whether it is needed.

communication_speech_act_id.description: #1968 verb-UX round 4 (SPEECH-ACT lens, Searle) — when set, the generated action's outcome_templates row carries this `communication_speech_act_id`, so the affordance SURFACES as a communication speech act while r_manipulate still EXECUTES the gated consequence normally via `manipulation_action_id` (mirrors compose.ts's ActorBehavior.communicationSpeechActId — the Persuasion 'directive' worked example). Omit for the legacy default: no speech-act framing.

grant_to.description: entity_key of the caster (already placed via spellkave_place_actor) granted the capability — or an ARRAY of entity_keys to grant the SAME capability to several actors in one call (#1968 finding B4: 'author once, grant twice' — e.g. two mechanically-identical monsters sharing one scimitar). The capability/action/affordance/outcome/consequence cluster is authored exactly ONCE regardless (keyed off the FIRST entry, which also becomes `defaultCaster` for any `[[actors]]`/entities the shape itself emits, e.g. Spawn's `def_instance`) — every entry gets its OWN `actor_capabilities` grant + `spatial_niche_attachments` row (attached to ITS OWN node, resolved independently per entity_key, exactly like the single-actor case). #1968 workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES the WHOLE grant set — an entity_key dropped from the array on a later call has its grant and attachment rows cleared, not left behind (mirrors every other satellite this verb folds).

reach.description: Closed PoC enum — only 'same_node' is wired (its own range_m default, see `range_m`).

range_m.description: Affordance range_m (metres, ADR-0053 metric embedding) — author via the ft() feet→metric helper (e.g. ft(5) for standard 5-ft melee reach), never a raw metre literal. Omit for the default range_m=0 (touch/same-node only).

target.description: #1968 US9 — a target concept beyond 'ForEachActorInRadius hits others in a radius'. Omit for the legacy default (`effect.write.primitive` must be 'ModifyResource', wrapped in `effect.shape`'s ForEachActorInRadius — unaffected by this param). 'self': the acting actor targets ITSELF (action_definitions.self_eligible=true, mirrors srd/cast_find_familiar's self_eligible=true) — MF-VAL-263 then requires SOME ModifyResource in the on_success chain; `effect.write.primitive: 'ModifyResource'` satisfies it on its own, but 'Spawn'/'Inscribe' need an explicit `cost` (else this tool errors BEFORE validation with a hint). 'place': the write lands at the actor's OWN place_node with NO target-actor selection and NO self-targeting at all (self_eligible stays false — MF-VAL-263 never engages, so no `cost` pool is required or accepted); only 'Spawn'/'Inscribe' support 'place' (no fixture idiom modifies a resource with neither an actor nor a self target).

action_class.description: action_definition_tag applied to the generated action (e.g. 'spell'). REQUIRED — has no default (#1968 finding A1): omitting it throws a named-param error rather than silently authoring a corrupt row. Overridden (not supplemented) by `tags` when that param is set.

pool.description: resource_definition_id debited on cast (e.g. a spell-slot pool).

amount.description: How much to debit per cast.

primitive.description: Closed PoC enum — only 'ForEachActorInRadius' is wired.

id.description: Closed PoC enum: 'core/area/node_ball' (topological — radius = ball_radius graph-edge hops, 0 = same node) or 'core/area/sphere' (metric — radius = radius_m). Other area shapes need direct authoring.

radius.description: node_ball: integer edge-hop radius. sphere: metric radius_m.

per_target_gate.description: Authored Bool DSL expression gating the write, e.g. 'd20 < 13' (a failed save) or 'd20 >= 13' (a hit). Omit for an ungated write. aoe (effect.shape set): gates the body PER SELECTED ACTOR. single-target (effect.shape omitted): gates the AFFORDANCE itself (a miss/failed-check skips the whole consequence — the attack-roll seam). ModifyResource only — MUST be omitted for 'Spawn'/'Inscribe'.

primitive.description: Closed PoC enum — the REAL kernel primitive names (#1968 US9/srd-migration round, never invented; verified against world-fixtures/srd/base/summon.toml + world-fixtures/core/base/affordances.toml + world-fixtures/srd/base/hold-monster.toml + world-fixtures/srd/base/lesser-restoration.toml + world-fixtures/srd/base/darkness.toml + world-fixtures/srd/base/acid-arrow.toml + world-fixtures/srd/base/moonbeam.toml + world-fixtures/srd/base/death-saves.toml): 'ModifyResource' (a resource/state delta — the original fireball-wired primitive), 'Spawn' (Brief 26 EffectPrimitive::Spawn — instantiate an entity_def at the actor's own node, the find_familiar shape; requires `offered_when.target`), 'Inscribe' (the raw FrameWriteOp::Inscribe trace idiom core/mark/core/pickup/core/drop use — a durable typed footprint, NO ModifyResource delta and NO companion definition row; requires `offered_when.target`), 'ApplyStatus' (lands a condition on the single TargetActor — the B9 Hold-Person/Hold-Monster/Bless-family shape; single-target only, no `offered_when.target`), 'RemoveCondition' (the INVERSE — deletes a matching target_condition row, the Lesser-Restoration cleanse shape; single-target only, no `offered_when.target`), 'EnvState' (#1968 verb-UX round 4 — the Darkness/Silence/Fog AMBIENT-EFFECT shape, compose.ts's 'env-state': the cast's ONLY write is an Inscribe{kind:'spatial_environment_state'} bool marker on the caster's cell (or the target cell — see `env_state_center`); this call auto-creates the backing spatial_state_definitions row, mirroring `cost.pool`'s auto-create; a SEPARATELY-authored consumer affordance reads target.state(env_state_id); single-target only, no `offered_when.target`), 'OutcomeGraph' (#1968 verb-UX round 4 — the branch-on-outcome shape, compose.ts's 'outcome-graph': the action's outcome invokes a graph whose `branches` (see that field) each carry their OWN ModifyResource(TargetActor, srd/hp, ...) consequence, selected by the first true edge guard in array order — unlike a gated single-target write, EVERY branch can apply an effect (a Melf's Acid Arrow miss still deals half damage); single-target only, no `offered_when.target`), 'ScheduledZone' (#1968 verb-UX round 5 — the TRUE LINGERING hazard shape, compose.ts's 'scheduled-zone' (ADR-0054): the cast's ONLY direct write is the SAME Inscribe{kind:'spatial_environment_state'} marker EnvState uses (auto-creates the backing spatial_state_definitions row, `zone_state_id`/`zone_intensity`/ `zone_visibility`/`zone_center` — see those fields); it ALSO schedules a subject-bound ScheduleAutonomyJob (`schedule` — repeats/frequency/liveness/source) that re-fires a SEPARATE, self-contained pulse consequence each round — a node-local ForEachActorInRadius (fixed radius, ball_radius 0) wrapping `effect.write.pulse`, which REUSES this same closed enum's two autonomy-clock-eligible bodies ('ModifyResource' damage/heal via `pulse.delta`, or 'ApplyStatus' condition via `pulse.condition`) rather than inventing a third write vocabulary; `effect.per_target_gate` (if set) gates the PULSE body per occupant (the save-negate seam — Stinking Cloud), not the affordance; single-target-only, no `offered_when.target`), 'Clock' (#1968 finding C2 — the SELF-TARGETED multi-ordinal clock shape, compose.ts's 'clock' (the death-saves death-and-dying pattern): unlike every OTHER primitive above (each writes a TargetActor or a radius-selected OTHER actor), a clock's every write targets the ACTING subject alone. `tallies` (see that field) — N bare ModifyResource(actor='Actor', ...) ordinals, authored first, array order = ordinal order — followed by `thresholds` (see that field) — M ForEachActorInRadius(node_ball, ball_radius 0) ordinals wrapping an ApplyStatus/RemoveCondition on 'Actor', reading the tallies' just-written state; requires `offered_when.target: 'self'` (a clock is inherently self-only — there is no 'hit others' reading of it) and needs no separate `cost` (the tallies themselves satisfy MF-VAL-263's on_success ModifyResource requirement); single-target-topology-only, no `effect.shape`/`effect.per_target_gate` (each threshold carries its OWN `when` instead of one shared per-target gate — `effect.per_target_gate`, if set, becomes the AFFORDANCE's own eligibility gate instead, e.g. "actor.status('dying') == true && ...", the same seam single-target's attack-roll gate reuses)). 'Spawn'/'Inscribe' are NOT FrameWriteOp arms nestable inside a ForEachActorInRadius body — they never combine with `effect.shape`/`effect.per_target_gate` (PoC boundary: only 'ModifyResource' selects actors in a radius). 'ApplyStatus'/'RemoveCondition'/'EnvState'/'OutcomeGraph'/'ScheduledZone'/'Clock' are single-target-only too (PoC boundary: no aoe condition/env-state/outcome-graph/scheduled-zone-CAST/clock pulse is wired — the scheduled-zone shape's OWN pulse is always the fixed node_ball-0 radius, never `effect.shape`) — they never combine with `effect.shape` either ('ScheduledZone' reuses `effect.per_target_gate` for its pulse's per-occupant gate instead, 'Clock' reuses it for the affordance's eligibility gate instead, see above).

resource.description: ModifyResource only: must already resolve to an authored resource_definitions row (workspace, live, or the active target) — this PoC does not auto-create write-target resources (only `cost.pool` auto-creates, see the tool description). aoe (effect.shape set): the resource every selected actor's body write targets. single-target (effect.shape omitted, #1968 verb-UX round 2): the resource the ONE TargetActor write targets — defaults to 'srd/hp'-shaped combat use but any already-authored resource/state works (e.g. a non-HP disposition state).

delta.description: ModifyResource only: authored Int DSL expression evaluated per target, e.g. '-d6'. aoe: applied to every selected actor. single-target: applied once, to the ONE TargetActor. Ignored (may be omitted) when `attacks` is set.

This sub-attack's authored Int DSL expression, self-gating its OWN attack roll (e.g. 'cond(d20 >= 11, 0 - (1d8 + 5), 0)') — a miss on THIS roll must resolve to 0, not skip the whole action (unlike the single-attack affordance-gated shape).

label.description: Human tag for this sub-attack (e.g. 'Rend'), report-only.

attacks.description: One entry per sub-attack (2+ for an SRD Multiattack, but generalises to any N) — see this field's own top-level description for the full shape.

entity_def.description: Spawn only: the entity_definitions catalog id to instantiate at the actor's own node (e.g. 'srd/monster/cat', mirroring srd/cast_find_familiar) — must already resolve (workspace or live); this PoC does not auto-create the blueprint.

trace_kind.description: Inscribe only: the trace's `kind` discriminant (e.g. 'puddle_mark') — an arbitrary authored string; unlike `resource`, this is NEVER ref-checked against a definitions row (core/mark's own 'scrape_marks' has none either — FrameWriteOp::Inscribe's own doc: 'a durable typed footprint without a resource delta').

content.description: Inscribe only: the trace's `payload_json` content — a JSON-encodable string describing the mark (e.g. '{"action":"relieve"}').

condition.description: ApplyStatus/RemoveCondition only: the condition_definitions condition_definition_id landed on (ApplyStatus) or deleted from (RemoveCondition) the single TargetActor — must already resolve (workspace, live, or the active target); this PoC does not auto-create the condition (use spellkave_define_condition first).

remove_source.description: RemoveCondition only: an exact source key to match (FrameWriteOp::RemoveCondition's `source_match: Exact`). Omit for the default 'Any' — source-agnostic removal (matches ANY target_condition row for `condition`, regardless of what applied it).

env_state_id.description: EnvState only: the spatial_state_definitions id this write flips (e.g. 'srd/darkness') — auto-created by this call as a BOOL state def with writer_policy 'world_interaction' (so the apply path may write it at cast time) and a long freshness, mirroring `cost.pool`'s auto-create; this PoC never requires it pre-authored. A separately-authored consumer affordance reads target.state(env_state_id) — this call does not author the consumer.

env_state_value.description: EnvState only: the bool value the marker Inscribe writes. Default true ('on').

env_state_center.description: EnvState only: 'actor' (default) writes the CASTER'S OWN cell (ActorSpatialRef — follows the caster, a Darkness-shaped ambient cast). 'target' anchors on the cast's TARGET cell (TargetSpatialRef) instead.

node.description: This branch's outcome_graph node id (e.g. 'hit'/'miss'; also the outcome/consequence id stem).

guard.description: This branch's edge guard predicate, evaluated root→node in array order — the FIRST true guard wins (e.g. 'd20 >= 13'); the LAST branch should carry a '1 == 1' fallthrough so some branch always selects.

delta.description: This branch's authored Int DSL expression — the ModifyResource delta its terminal node's consequence applies when selected (e.g. '0 - 4d4'), written against `subject`'s `resource`.

label.description: Human tag for this branch, report-only.

subject.description: This branch's own write subject — a kernel symbolic actor ref: 'TargetActor' (default, the damage-against-target shape every prior branch authored) or 'Actor' (the CASTER, e.g. a defeat-consequence XP credit back to the attacker — playable-fighter-l1-20 D-1). Omit to keep today's byte-identical shape.

resource.description: This branch's own write resource — must already resolve to an authored resource_definitions row, same rule as the top-level `resource` field. Defaults to 'srd/hp'. Omit to keep today's byte-identical shape.

branches.description: OutcomeGraph only: one entry per branch arm (2+ — see this field's own top-level description). Required, and must be non-empty, when effect.write.primitive is 'OutcomeGraph'.

zone_state_id.description: ScheduledZone only: the spatial_state_definitions id the marker Inscribe (and every pulse) reads/writes (e.g. 'srd/hazard/cloudkill') — auto-created by this call as an INT state def with writer_policy 'world_interaction' and a long freshness, mirroring EnvState's `env_state_id` auto-create (and `cost.pool`'s). Required when effect.write.primitive is 'ScheduledZone'.

zone_intensity.description: ScheduledZone only: the documentary int value the marker Inscribe stamps (e.g. the spell's damage magnitude — Cloudkill's 5d8 stamps 5). Default 0. Never read by the pulse itself (the pulse's own damage/condition comes from `pulse.delta`/`pulse.condition`) — purely an observable marker value.

zone_visibility.description: ScheduledZone only: the marker Inscribe's visibility class. Default 'Public'.

zone_center.description: ScheduledZone only: 'actor' (default) anchors the marker AND every pulse on the CASTER'S CURRENT cell each fire (ActorSpatialRef — a mobile aura that follows the caster). 'target' anchors on the cast's TARGET cell instead (TargetSpatialRef — the captured anchor_place_node_id stays FIXED even if the caster moves; the faithful 'dropped at range' hazard every shipped scheduled-zone spell today uses — Cloudkill/Moonbeam/Stinking Cloud/the scheduled-damage-zone batch). Mirrors EnvState's `env_state_center` — same two-value anchor concept, kept as its own field because it is scoped to a different write primitive.

repeats.description: How many rounds the pulse re-fires — bounds the duration (a subject-bound actor-reaching autonomy job MUST be bounded, server fence + MF-VAL-249). Default 10 (SRD's common 'concentration up to 1 minute' → 10 one-tick rounds).

frequency_ms.description: Fiction-millisecond period between pulses. Default 6000 (fires every round).

requires_subject_alive.description: Whether the zone dissipates if the caster's entity is removed. Default false (the zone lingers its full duration regardless — the SRD Cloudkill/Moonbeam behaviour). Set true for a concentration-style hazard that ends with its caster.

source.description: The cancel-by-source/provenance key stamped on the runtime autonomy_job — author with the {Actor}/{ResponsibleSubject}/{tick} placeholders (ADR-0055 D-3), e.g. '<bundle>/<id>/{Actor}/{tick}', so the scheduler interpolates a PER-CAST-UNIQUE job_id at cast time (two concurrent casts never collide on the autonomy_job PK). Omit for the compose.ts legacy default ('srd/<id>', UNqualified by `bundle` — pass this explicitly for any non-'srd' bundle).

schedule.description: ScheduledZone only: the ADR-0054 autonomy-pulse cadence + provenance. Every field optional — omit the whole object for compose.ts's defaults (repeats 10, frequency_ms 6000, requires_subject_alive false, source 'srd/<id>').

primitive.description: The scheduled pulse's OWN per-round frame_write body (wrapped in a fixed node-local ForEachActorInRadius, ball_radius 0, by clusterRows — never `effect.shape`) — REUSES this tool's two autonomy-clock-eligible write shapes rather than a new vocabulary: 'ModifyResource' (a damage/heal delta on 'srd/hp', the Cloudkill/Moonbeam/scheduled-damage-zone-batch shape) or 'ApplyStatus' (lands a condition on each occupant, the Stinking Cloud save-or-condition shape — #958 admits ApplyStatus to the subject-bound autonomy fence).

delta.description: pulse.primitive 'ModifyResource' only: the authored Int DSL expression applied to EVERY occupant's srd/hp each pulse (e.g. 'cond(d20 >= 13, 0 - (5d8 / 2), 0 - 5d8)' for save-for-half — fold the save into the delta the same way single-target/aoe do). Required when pulse.primitive is 'ModifyResource'.

condition.description: pulse.primitive 'ApplyStatus' only: the condition_definitions id landed on every occupant whose `effect.per_target_gate` passes (e.g. 'srd/poisoned') — must already resolve (workspace, live, or the active target); this PoC does not auto-create it (use spellkave_define_condition first). Required when pulse.primitive is 'ApplyStatus'.

pulse.description: ScheduledZone only: the pulse's own write. Required when effect.write.primitive is 'ScheduledZone' — a zone with no pulse body would schedule a job that fires nothing.

resource.description: Clock only: the resource_definitions id this tally ordinal's bare ModifyResource(actor='Actor', ...) reads/writes — must already resolve (workspace, live, or the active target); this PoC does not auto-create tally resources (use spellkave_define_resource first, same posture as effect.write.resource).

predicate.description: Clock only: an authored Bool DSL expression — when set, this ordinal's delta_source becomes 'cond(<predicate>, <delta ?? "1">, 0)', the increment-on-condition idiom every tally-split ordinal needs (e.g. "actor.stat('death_save_last_roll') >= 10" to tally a success). Omit for a raw (non-conditional) `delta` expression instead — the scratch-cell-capture idiom a clock's FIRST ordinal often needs (e.g. "d20 - actor.stat('death_save_last_roll')", a set-via-delta that lands exactly on a fresh roll). Exactly one of `predicate`/`delta` must convey the real expression: set `predicate` alone for a plain +1-on-condition tally, `delta` alone for a raw capture, or both when the increment amount is not 1.

delta.description: Clock only: with `predicate` set, the increment amount (default '1') — the expression becomes 'cond(<predicate>, <delta>, 0)'. With `predicate` OMITTED, this is the WHOLE raw delta_source expression verbatim (the scratch-cell-capture idiom — see `predicate`'s own doc). Required when `predicate` is omitted.

tallies.description: Clock only: one entry per self-targeted tally ordinal, authored FIRST (array order = ordinal order, before every `thresholds` entry) — see this field's own top-level description. Required, non-empty, when effect.write.primitive is 'Clock'.

when.description: Clock only: this threshold ordinal's own ForEachActorInRadius(node_ball, ball_radius 0) predicate_source, evaluated against the POST-tally state (this ordinal runs after every `tallies` entry) — e.g. "actor.stat('death_save_failures') >= 3", or an OR-branched short-circuit like a nat-20 immediate-stabilize check. A bare ApplyStatus/RemoveCondition carries no delta/predicate of its own to fold a `cond(...)` into, so this wrapper's own predicate_source is the only way to gate one — safe here specifically because every `tallies` ordinal already wrote 'Actor' alone (never a co-located bystander).

apply_status.description: Clock only: the condition_definitions id this threshold lands on 'Actor' when `when` is true — must already resolve (workspace, live, or the active target); this PoC does not auto-create it (use spellkave_define_condition first). Exactly one of `apply_status`/`remove_condition` must be set per threshold entry.

remove_condition.description: Clock only: the condition_definitions id this threshold REMOVES from 'Actor' when `when` is true (the inverse of `apply_status`) — must already resolve. Exactly one of `apply_status`/`remove_condition` must be set per threshold entry.

remove_condition_source.description: Clock + `remove_condition` only: an exact source key to match (RemoveCondition's `source_match: Exact`). Omit for the default 'Any' — source-agnostic removal.

thresholds.description: Clock only: one entry per self-targeted threshold ordinal, authored AFTER every `tallies` entry (array order = ordinal order) — see this field's own top-level description. Required, non-empty, when effect.write.primitive is 'Clock'.

bind_to_definition.description: An already-authored entity_definitions catalog id (workspace, live, or the active target — same 3-way resolution as the placement tools' `entity_def`) that inherits this call's capability at instance birth via entity_definition_initial_capability. This PoC does not auto-create the definition (use spellkave_define_entity_type first).

entity_key.description: The proof instance's fully-qualified entity_key, e.g. 'srd/actor/polar-bear-def'.

name.description: entities.name / actors.name for the proof instance.

node.description: An already-authored place_node id the proof instance is placed at. Omit to default to the resolved caster node (`grant_to`'s own node) — the niche this behavior's capability attaches is already anchored there.

tools.name: spellkave_define_entity_type
tools.label: Define Entity Type (verb)
tools.description: Author ONE entity_definitions catalog blueprint (+ its entity_definition_tag/initial_state/initial_capability/initial_condition/initial_containment/initial_equipment satellites) in a single call — the #1968 53%-of-authored-rows cluster, folding what would otherwise be a per-tag/per-seed spellkave_write_rows call each. Self-scaffolds the [[bundles]] header if `bundle` has none yet. This authors the CATALOG blueprint only (placement tools instantiate entities that may reference it via entity_def). #1968 workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES the row + EVERY satellite wholesale (fewer tags/seeds on a re-run means the stale ones are gone, not left behind). initial_containment/initial_equipment are structural (each spawns a child instance), not a flat-value copy like the other three satellites — the equipment/containment graph is cycle-checked server-side (MF-VAL-314) at admission, not re-validated here.

bundle.description: bundle_id stamped on every generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (#1968 smart default).

id.description: Local entity_def_id stem; the full id is '<bundle>/<id>' (e.g. bundle='core', id='item/sword' -> 'core/item/sword'). May itself contain '/' for sub-namespacing (matches the corpus convention, e.g. 'npc/caravan', 'class/barbarian').

display_name.description: entity_definitions.display_name. Omit to derive a title-cased `id` (#1968 smart default).

description.description: entity_definitions.description (#1968 first-class column).

stackable.description: entity_definitions.stackable — may authored instances use quantity>1 (default false).

grants_capability_while_equipped.description: CSV capability ids granted to the bearer while it equips an entity of this definition (default '').

grants_capability_while_present_in_locat.description: CSV capability ids granted to entities at locations where an entity of this definition is present (default '').

slot_compatibility_predicate.description: Closed three-form slot-compatibility grammar (not spellkave-dsl); '' or 'true' means any slot, 'false' means none, slot_id == <quoted id> means only that slot.

state.description: object_state_definitions OR resource_definitions state_id (MF-VAL-253 accepts either catalog) seeded as an object_state row onto every placed instance of this entity_def. Visibility caveat: a resource-only id has no default_visibility authoring surface, so the seeded row falls back to Public — author a parallel object_state_definitions row when Local/Hidden visibility is wanted.

value_bool.description: Bool carrier (schema default true when neither value_int nor value_text is set). Carrier precedence at commit: value_int > value_text > value_bool.

value_text.description: Text carrier — commit precedence between value_int and value_bool.

initial_states.description: entity_definition_initial_state rows — seeded onto every placed instance at admission/spawn.

capability.description: capability_definitions capability_id granted unconditionally to every placed instance of this entity_def (an entity_definition_initial_capability seed row).

condition.description: condition_definitions condition_definition_id seeded onto every placed instance of this entity_def.

duration_ticks.description: Ticks until auto-expiry; 0 or omitted = permanent (schema default 0).

initial_conditions.description: entity_definition_initial_condition rows — conditions born active on every placed instance.

contained_entity_def_id.description: entity_def_id of the child instance spawned and carried loose (entity_containment, slot_id = '') on every placed/spawned instance of this entity_def (an entity_definition_initial_containment seed row). Structural, not a flat-value copy: the child's OWN initial_* seeds apply to it first (recursion). The containment/equipment graph is cycle-checked server-side (MF-VAL-314) at admission.

quantity.description: Stack-vs-instance-count rule (ADR-0028 D-6): when the contained definition is stackable, ONE instance is spawned carrying this as its stack count; otherwise this many separate instances are spawned. Default 1.

initial_containment.description: entity_definition_initial_containment rows — each spawns a child instance carried loose (no equipment slot) on every placed/spawned instance. Structural, not a flat-value copy; MF-VAL-314 cycle-checked server-side at admission (not duplicated here).

equipped_entity_def_id.description: entity_def_id of the child instance spawned and equipped into `slot_id` on every placed/spawned instance of this entity_def (an entity_definition_initial_equipment seed row) — a child, one slot, implicit quantity 1. The containment/equipment graph is cycle-checked server-side (MF-VAL-314) at admission, and the equipped definition's slot_compatibility_predicate is checked at commit (MF-VAL-311/-312/-313).

slot_id.description: equipment_slot_definitions slot_id the spawned child is equipped into.

initial_equipment.description: entity_definition_initial_equipment rows — each spawns a child instance and equips it into the named slot on every placed/spawned instance. Structural, not a flat-value copy; MF-VAL-314 cycle-checked server-side at admission (not duplicated here).

tools.name: spellkave_define_roll_table
tools.label: Define Roll Table (verb)

bundle.description: bundle_id stamped on every generated row (roll_table_entries excepted — that row kind carries no bundle_id column). Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (#1968 smart default).

id.description: Local roll_table_id stem; the full id is '<bundle>/<id>' (e.g. bundle='core', id='d20' -> 'core/d20').

display_name.description: roll_tables.display_name. Omit to derive a title-cased `id` (#1968 smart default).

result_kind.description: roll_tables.result_kind — an open string (the corpus already uses more than one value, e.g. 'int', 'outcome_graph'); no closed PoC enum.

description.description: roll_tables.description (#1968 first-class column).

result_ref.description: roll_table_entries.result_ref — the drawn value/reference text for this entry.

tags.description: One roll_table_entry_tag row per tag, for THIS entry.

tools.name: spellkave_define_condition
tools.label: Define Condition (verb)
tools.description: Author ONE condition_definitions row (+ condition_definition_tag satellites) in a single call, optionally ALSO authoring the condition_remove_policy_definitions/stacking_discipline_definitions vocabulary rows it references (shared cross-condition vocabulary — upserted by their OWN id, never duplicated, mirroring the server's own upsert-in-place discipline for these two kinds, ADR-0085) and any modifier_templates (+ modifier_template_tag) it needs (also upserted by their own modifier_template_id). DSL-bearing fields (gate_predicate_source, hooks[]._source, remove_predicate_source, *_outcome_source, predicate_source, modifier_expression_source) are passed through as free text verbatim — single-parse discipline is the server's job. Self-scaffolds the [[bundles]] header if `bundle` has none yet. #1968 workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES the condition row + its tag satellites wholesale (fewer tags on a re-run means the stale ones are gone, not left behind).

bundle.description: bundle_id stamped on every generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (#1968 smart default).

display_name.description: condition_definitions.display_name. Omit to derive a title-cased `id` (#1968 smart default).

description.description: condition_definitions.description (#1968 first-class column).

gate_predicate_source.description: DSL Bool expression gating condition-triggered modifier application (default '').

grants_capability_while_active.description: Capability ids GRANTED to the bearer while this condition is active (default []). Enforced in capability_ids_for_actor; use this rather than a status when the thing granted is an ability to act, because affordance_template.capability_id is a structural gate a status cannot reproduce.

suppresses_capability_while_active.description: Capability ids SUPPRESSED on the bearer AS AN ACTOR while this condition is active (default []). Suppression beats a grant of the same id. Applies to the bearer's own attempts to act only — it never makes the bearer an illegal TARGET, so a spell like Speak with Dead stays authorable against a corpse that cannot itself speak.

implies.description: condition_definitions.implies — cascade edges (each id is ALSO applied when this condition is applied).

detail_filter_source.description: Inline-DSL Bool sub-expression gating which event instances this hook fires for. Passed through verbatim (single-parse discipline is the server's job, not this verb's).

expression_source.description: Inline-DSL Int sub-expression evaluated when the hook fires. Passed through verbatim.

remove_time_policy.description: condition_definitions.remove_time_policy — REFERENCE an existing policy id (default 'core/remove_policy/independent_lifetime'). Pass `remove_policy` instead to ALSO author the row.

id.description: The FULL condition_remove_policy_definitions policy_id (cross-bundle vocabulary — e.g. 'core/remove_policy/independent_lifetime'; NOT bundle-prefixed by this verb, unlike `id`).

display_name.description: condition_remove_policy_definitions.display_name. Omit to derive a title-cased `id` (#1968 smart default).

remove_predicate_source.description: DSL Bool expression; the removal path evaluates this instead of branching on the policy id.

stacking_rule.description: condition_definitions.stacking_rule — REFERENCE an existing discipline id (default 'core/stacking/single'). Pass `stacking` instead to ALSO author the row.

id.description: The FULL stacking_discipline_definitions discipline_id (cross-bundle vocabulary — e.g. 'core/stacking/single'; NOT bundle-prefixed by this verb, unlike `id`).

display_name.description: stacking_discipline_definitions.display_name. Omit to derive a title-cased `id` (#1968 smart default).

stack_count_outcome_source.description: Int-valued DSL expression over the existing row state (facts: stack_count, expires_at_tick, world_tick).

expires_at_tick_outcome_source.description: Int-valued DSL expression; -1 means 'leave the existing expiry unchanged'.

modifier_template_id.description: condition_definitions.modifier_template_id — REFERENCE an existing modifier (default ''). Omit when `modifiers` has EXACTLY one entry (auto-wired to it); REQUIRED when `modifiers` has more than one entry (which one is the FK, otherwise ambiguous).

id.description: Local modifier_templates id stem; full id '<bundle>/<id>'.

display_name.description: modifier_templates.display_name. Omit to derive a title-cased `id` (#1968 smart default).

applies_to.description: modifier_templates.applies_to — the composition-axis vocabulary id (an authored modifier_target_definitions row, e.g. 'ResolutionCheck'; open string).

modifier_expression_source.description: DSL expression producing the modifier's magnitude.

delta_kind.description: modifier_templates.delta_kind (default 'Plus') — the validator's OWN closed vocabulary (MF-VAL-243), not a PoC-narrower enum.

replace_template_id.description: Required (by the validator) when delta_kind='Replace' — the modifier_template id this one replaces.

tags.description: One modifier_template_tag row per tag, for THIS modifier.

modifiers.description: modifier_templates rows (+ their modifier_template_tag satellites) authored in this call.

tools.name: spellkave_define_niche
tools.label: Define Niche (verb)
tools.description: Author ONE niche_definitions row (+ niche_definition_tag satellites, + spatial_niche_attachments binding it to place nodes/edges) in a single call. bundle.description: bundle_id stamped on every generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (#1968 smart default).

display_name.description: niche_definitions.display_name. Omit to derive a title-cased `id` (#1968 smart default).

tools.name: spellkave_define_affordance
tools.label: Define Affordance (verb)
tools.description: #1968 verb-UX round 6: author ONE niche-triggered ENVIRONMENTAL affordance — an outcome_templates row + an affordance_templates row referencing an ALREADY-authored `niche_id`/`capability_id` — in a single call, with NO actor grant (contrast spellkave_define_behavior, which always binds a capability to a `grant_to` caster). The US5-7 live-dungeon pressure-plate trap shape: 'any actor holding an existing capability (e.g. core/walk) that steps onto an existing niche triggers this'. Self-scaffolds the [[bundles]] header if `bundle` has none yet. #1968 workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES both rows wholesale.

bundle.description: bundle_id stamped on every generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (#1968 smart default).

id.description: Local affordance key stem — derives template_id '<bundle>/<id>/affordance' and outcome_template_id '<bundle>/<id>/outcome'.

niche_id.description: affordance_templates.niche_id — an ALREADY-authored niche_definitions id (workspace, live, or the active target, e.g. via spellkave_define_niche) this call never creates — the trigger surface (a trap/trigger niche, e.g. a pressure plate).

capability_id.description: affordance_templates.capability_id — an ALREADY-authored capability_definitions id (workspace, live, or the active target, e.g. 'core/walk') this call never creates — the pre-existing capability any qualifying actor already holds (no NEW grant is authored by this call).

display_name.description: Overrides the derived title-cased `id` for BOTH the outcome and affordance rows.

predicate_source.description: affordance_templates.predicate_source — the deterministic ELIGIBILITY gate for whether this affordance offers (e.g. a capability/state check like 'target.stat("srd/ac") >= 1'). A stochastic comparison here (e.g. 'd20 >= 13') is treated as satisfied at materialise time and never gates offer (#1891) — author dice on the action's resolution_predicate_source (resolution_mode = 'Stochastic') instead. Omit for an ungated trigger (predicate_bool = true).

outcome_expression_source.description: outcome_templates.outcome_expression_source — invokes a pre-authored effect (e.g. "invoke_outcome_graph('<bundle>/<id>/graph')"). Exactly ONE of `outcome_expression_source`/`manipulation_action_id` is required — an affordance with neither would trigger nothing.

manipulation_action_id.description: outcome_templates.manipulation_action_id — executes a pre-authored action_definitions row instead (the darkness-consumer idiom, packages/spellkave-srd/src/author/author-darkness.ts's `act_in_dark`). Exactly ONE of `outcome_expression_source`/`manipulation_action_id` is required.

tools.name: spellkave_define_capability
tools.label: Define Capability (verb)
tools.description: Author ONE capability_definitions row (+ capability_definition_tag satellites) in a single call — the #1968 verb-UX round's named missing bare-vocabulary verb. Self-scaffolds the [[bundles]] header if `bundle` has none yet. capability_definitions is referenced from MANY affordance_templates/action_definitions rows (not satellite-owned by a single parent) — those stay on spellkave_write_rows/spellkave_define_behavior, whichever fits the calling context. #1968 workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES the row + its tag satellite wholesale (fewer tags on a re-run means the stale ones are gone, not left behind).

bundle.description: bundle_id stamped on every generated row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (#1968 smart default).

id.description: Local capability_id stem; the full id is '<bundle>/<id>' (e.g. bundle='core', id='walk' -> 'core/walk'). A handful of corpus capability ids are DELIBERATELY cross-namespace (e.g. 'frontier.apply_manifest' under bundle_id='core') — this verb always derives '<bundle>/<id>', so a cross-namespace id stays on spellkave_write_rows (mirrors spellkave_define_entity_type's own cross-namespace carve-out).

actor_kind.description: capability_definitions.actor_kind — an open string (the corpus already uses more than one value, e.g. 'entity', 'operator'); no closed PoC enum.

display_name.description: capability_definitions.display_name. Omit to derive a title-cased `id` (#1968 smart default).

description.description: capability_definitions.description — REQUIRED (unlike every OTHER verb's optional `description?`): CapabilityDefinitionRow kept its own PRE-EXISTING required description column through the #1968 description-column decision (no `#[serde(default)]` in the schema); omitting it would author an invalid row, not merely a less-documented one (same carve-out as spellkave_define_niche's own required `description`).

default_visibility.description: capability_definitions.default_visibility — the ADR-0120 read-visibility default concrete grants inherit unless overridden. Omit to default 'Public' (#1968 smart default — matches the schema's own `default_public()` serde default).

tools.name: spellkave_define_consequence
tools.label: Define Consequence (verb)
tools.description: Author ONE consequence_templates row (+ its consequence_frame_writes satellites, in authored order) in a single call, with NO actor grant (contrast spellkave_define_behavior, which always binds its generated consequence to a `grant_to` caster's action cluster). Self-scaffolds the [[bundles]] header if `bundle` has none yet. #1968 workspace idempotency: re-authoring the SAME bundle+id REPLACES the row + every consequence_frame_writes row wholesale (fewer frame_writes on a re-run means the stale ones are gone, not left behind).

bundle.description: bundle_id stamped on the consequence_templates row. Omit to fall back to `context.defaultBundle` (#1968 smart default).

id.description: Local consequence_template_id stem; the full id is '<bundle>/<id>' (e.g. bundle='core', id='pickup/success' -> 'core/pickup/success').

effect_ref.description: consequence_templates.effect_refs_csv — an already-authored effect_definitions id this consequence invokes (e.g. a scheduled-zone/summon effect). The corpus never joins more than one id here despite the column's '_csv' name — a single ref, not a real CSV list. Omit for a consequence with no effect_definitions reference.

description.description: consequence_templates.description (#1968 first-class column).

frame_writes.description: consequence_frame_writes rows, in AUTHORED order — each a raw FrameWriteOp body object (e.g. {Inscribe: {...}}, {ModifyResource: {...}}, {PickupTargetItem: {...}}), mirroring spellkave_write_rows' own untyped row shape (the closed Rust FrameWriteOp enum is never modeled in TypeBox here). `ordinal` (0-based) is derived from array position — never hand-specified.

tools.name: spellkave_define_action
tools.label: Define Action (verb)
tools.description: Author ONE action_definitions row (+ action_definition_tag satellites) in a single call, with NO actor grant (contrast spellkave_define_behavior, which always binds its generated action to a `grant_to` caster). `required_capability` must already resolve (workspace, live, or the active target) — this verb never auto-creates it (use spellkave_define_capability first).
